Night eating behavior was moderately associated with poorer subjective sleep quality and remained significantly associated with PSQI scores after adjustment for measured sociodemographic and lifestyle factors. Although BMI showed weak unadjusted associations with sleep quality and night eating behavior, its association with sleep quality was not statistically significant in the fully adjusted model. These findings highlight the relevance of night eating-related symptoms to subjective sleep quality in adult women, without establishing a causal relationship.

papers.title: Effects of Heat-Killed Lactiplantibacillus plantarum L-137 on Menopause-Related Outcomes and Gut Barrier-Related Biomarkers in Japanese Women: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Menopause-related issues-such as mood disturbance, hot flashes, and sleep disturbance-are thought to be influenced not only by hormonal changes but also by everyday stress and gut barrier-related host responses. Heat-killed Lactiplantibacillus plantarum L-137 (HK L-137) has shown immunomodulatory and gut barrier-related effects, but clinical evidence for its effects in menopausal women is limited. We investigated whether HK L-137 intake affects menopause-related outcomes and gut barrier-related biomarkers in women reporting daily stress. Methods: We conducted a 12-week randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-group trial in healthy Japanese women aged 45-69 years who self-reported daily stress (UMIN000055687). Participants were randomly assigned to receive one tablet containing 10 mg HK L-137 or placebo daily. Mood state, menopausal symptoms, and sleep quality-as menopause-related outcomes-and gut barrier-related biomarkers were assessed at baseline and week 12. Results: A total of 121 participants were included, and 119 completed the study. No significant between-group differences were observed in the questionnaire scores of mood state, menopausal symptoms, or sleep quality. Changes in serum soluble CD14 (sCD14) and lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) differed significantly between groups, favoring the HK L-137 group (p = 0.020 and p = 0.010, respectively). In the prespecified subgroup with higher baseline levels of negative mood, HK L-137 significantly improved hot flashes item and sleep maintenance score, and was associated with favorable changes in sCD14, LDH, and body mass index versus placebo. No intervention-related safety concerns were identified. Conclusions: HK L-137 favorably affected sCD14 and LDH in the overall analysis and improved selected menopause-related outcomes in women with higher baseline levels of negative mood. These findings suggest a possible role of gut barrier-related host responses associated with microbial translocation.

papers.title: Mediterranean Diet, Physical Activity, and Sleep in Endometriosis: An Age-Comparable Case-Control Study with Exploratory Machine Learning Discrimination.
papers.abstract: Diet, physical activity, and sleep have been proposed as modulators of endometriosis, yet most evidence comes from studies in which cases are much older than controls, confounding lifestyle comparisons by age. We compared these profiles against controls of closer reproductive age and, as a secondary aim, explored how far self-reported data discriminate endometriosis. Cross-sectional case-control study of 177 women: 77 with self-reported, procedure-confirmed endometriosis recruited through a patient association and 100 controls consecutively enrolled from the general adult population. Measures included Mediterranean diet adherence (PREDIMED-14), physical activity (IPAQ), pain scales, menstrual quality of life (CVM-22) and the Epworth Sleepiness Scale. Analyses used age-adjusted logistic regression with Benjamini-Hochberg correction; three machine learning algorithms were evaluated with cross-validation. Mediterranean diet adherence and physical activity did not differ between groups; body mass index was modestly lower in cases, and daytime sleepiness was marginally higher but not after age adjustment. Of the 13 testable dietary items, only sofrito (vegetables slowly cooked in extra-virgin olive oil) survived correction, being reported less often by cases. Menstrual quality of life was markedly worse in cases. Discrimination (best AUC-ROC 0.933) reflected concurrent symptoms rather than nutrition: restricted to antecedent and dietary variables it reached only 0.67-0.73. Once age and multiple testing were accounted for, diet and physical activity did not distinguish women with endometriosis from controls. The lower sofrito intake is a single-item, cross-sectional finding that should be regarded as hypothesis-generating and requires independent validation.

papers.title: Stress, Depression, and Purpose-Specific Use of Dietary Supplements and Over-the-Counter Preparations: A Cross-Sectional Study of 120,000 Polish Adults.
papers.abstract: Dietary supplements and over-the-counter (OTC) preparations are widely used to self-manage stress, low mood, and disturbed sleep. Population research has treated such use as one undifferentiated behaviour. We examined whether stress and affective burden co-occur with supplement and OTC use in a purpose-specific way and how they relate to self-medication and primary-care contact. We analysed cross-sectional data from the National Test of Poles' Health (non-probability, self-selected web survey; wave 5, 2024; N = 120,000), with trend analyses across five cross-sections (2020-2024). Survey-weighted logistic regression related four indicators of psychological burden to purpose-specific use of mood-, sleep-, and memory-targeted products, with a symptom-by-purpose matrix, age- and sex-stratified replication, and E-values. Mood-product use rose along a gradient of psychological burden, from frequent stress (adjusted odds ratios [aOR] 1.80, 95% confidence intervals [CI] 1.72-1.88) through work-related exhaustion (2.17, 2.08-2.26) and poor self-rated mental health (2.44, 2.34-2.55) to a lifetime depression diagnosis (2.53, 2.41-2.65). A lifetime depression diagnosis also co-occurred with sleep (1.92, 1.83-2.01) and memory-product use (1.77, 1.69-1.85), while multivitamin and hair/skin use stayed flat (aOR ≈ 1.0). In this subgroup (n = 21,793), targeted use co-occurred with OTC self-medication (mood 1.70, 1.59-1.83; sleep 1.61, 1.50-1.73) without reduced primary-care contact. Associations were observed in both broad age strata (≤54 vs. >54 years) and both sexes (E-values 4.3-9.5). Purpose-specific use rose across the five cross-sections. Supplement use tracks stress and affective burden in a purpose-specific way and, among respondents reporting a lifetime physician diagnosis of depression, accompanies OTC self-medication. This pattern marks a group whose self-management concentrates on preparations with limited trial support. The scope of these findings is set by two features: the depression measure is lifetime, not an assessment of current symptoms, and the questionnaire recorded the purpose of use, not the product identity, ingredients or dose.

papers.title: Is Earlier Always Better? Early Versus Later Time-Restricted Eating, Body Composition, and Exercise Performance: A Narrative Review.
papers.abstract: Background: Time-restricted eating (TRE) confines daily food intake to a consistent window that may occur early (eTRE) or later in the day (delayed TRE, dTRE). Whether timing differentially affects body composition and exercise performance, and whether exercise training modifies these effects, remains unclear. Methods: PubMed, Google Scholar, and reference lists were searched. Twenty-three intervention studies were narratively synthesized by timing comparison and exercise context, with study-level methodological appraisal. Results: Eight studies directly compared earlier and later windows. None favored the later window for body composition. Greater weight or fat loss with eTRE came from one crossover trial and two non-randomized comparisons, whereas the randomized parallel-group trials, including the largest, detected no difference. With structured training, TRE reduced fat mass more than training alone in four of six trials, regardless of window type; lean-mass comparisons were imprecise. No direct comparison detected timing differences in strength, muscular endurance, or aerobic outcomes, but estimates were imprecise. Greater sprint power after dTRE in one crossover trial may reflect test-day feeding, learning, or order effects. Conclusions: Earlier eating was not consistently better, but timing cannot be considered irrelevant. Trials crossing window timing with controlled energy intake and matched training are needed.

papers.title: Planetary Health Diet, Obesity and Sleep Quality in Italian Adults.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sleep and diet have been demonstrated to be interconnected factors playing an important role in human health. However, the relationship between sustainable dietary patterns, sleep, and obesity remains to be fully elucidated. This study investigated the association between adherence to the Planetary Health Diet (PHD) and sleep quality among Italian adults, while also exploring the potential role of weight status in this relationship. Methods: This observational study included 1936 Italian adults. Dietary intake was assessed using a validated food-frequency questionnaire (FFQ), and adherence to the PHD was evaluated using a validated index. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Multivariable logistic regression analyses were conducted to examine the associations between PHD adherence and sleep quality. Results: Among 1936 participants, higher PHDI adherence was associated with greater odds of adequate sleep quality. Compared with the lowest quartile, participants in the highest PHDI quartile had 65% higher odds of adequate sleep quality (OR: 1.65; 95% CI: 1.20, 2.28); significant associations were also observed for sleep disturbance and self-rated sleep quality, whereas sleep duration, sleep efficiency, and sleep-medication use were not associated with PHDI adherence. Associations were more pronounced among participants with overweight or obesity, in whom the highest quartile was associated with more than twice the odds of adequate sleep quality (OR: 2.40; 95% CI: 1.46, 3.95). Additional domain-specific associations were observed in this subgroup, whereas no significant association with overall sleep quality was found among normal-weight participants. Conclusions: Greater adherence to the PHD was associated with better overall and self-rated sleep quality among Italian adults, with stronger associations observed among individuals with overweight or obesity. These findings suggest that adherence to a healthy and sustainable dietary pattern may be related to better sleep health, particularly among individuals with excess body weight.

papers.title: Nutraceutical, Nutritional and Phytotherapeutic Interventions for Neuropsychiatric Disorders Associated with Intellectual Disability: Mechanisms and Clinical Evidence.
papers.abstract: Intellectual disability (ID) is frequently accompanied by a range of neuropsychiatric and neurological comorbidities, including anxiety, depression, autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), sleep disturbances, and epilepsy. Conventional pharmacological treatments often provide partial relief and may be associated with adverse effects, prompting interest in adjunctive strategies such as phytotherapy. This review examines the current evidence on selected plant-derived compounds-particularly Crocus sativus (saffron), Bacopa monnieri, Curcuma longa (curcumin), and other botanicals-in the management of disorders associated with ID. Mechanistic pathways, clinical evidence, and safety considerations are critically discussed. Although some phytotherapeutic interventions have shown preliminary evidence of potential benefit and may modulate pathways involving neuroinflammation, oxidative stress, and neurotransmitter function, direct clinical evidence in individuals with ID remains limited. Further well-designed randomized controlled trials, particularly in ID-specific populations, are needed to establish efficacy, safety, optimal dosing, and clinical applicability.

papers.title: Exploring Relationships Between Multimodal Lifestyle Factors, Inflammatory Biomarkers, and Pain Processing in Women with Fibromyalgia: An Exploratory Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Fibromyalgia is a chronic pain condition characterised by altered pain processing, widespread pain, and symptoms including sleep disturbance, fatigue, and psychological distress. Emerging evidence suggests that modifiable multimodal lifestyle factors may influence inflammation and pain mechanisms; however, the relationships between multimodal lifestyle factors, systemic inflammatory biomarkers, and pain processing remain poorly understood. In this study we aimed to investigate the associations between lifestyle factors, inflammatory biomarkers, and experimental and clinical pain outcomes in women with fibromyalgia. Methods: Women with fibromyalgia were invited to participate in this exploratory cross-sectional study. Lifestyle factors included diet, perceived stress, sleep, physical activity, heart rate variability, and BMI. Plasma IL-6, IL-10, and TNF-α were measured. Pain outcomes included quantitative sensory testing and patient-reported outcome measures. Spearman's rank correlations and multiple linear regression analyses adjusted for age and disease duration were performed. Bootstrap 95% confidence intervals were calculated for all estimates, and False Discovery Rate (FDR) corrections using the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure were applied as a sensitivity analysis. Results: Twenty patients were included. Correlation analyses demonstrated that higher perceived stress was strongly associated with greater fibromyalgia impact (r = 0.68, p < 0.001, n = 20), central sensitization (r = 0.67, p < 0.001, n = 20), and current pain intensity (r = 0.64, p = 0.002, n = 20). A more pro-inflammatory diet was positively associated with IL-6 (r = 0.46, p = 0.04, n = 20) and IL-10 (r = 0.47, p = 0.10, n = 13), while higher TNF-α concentrations were associated with lower pressure pain thresholds (overall; r = -0.55, p = 0.021, n = 19; tibialis: r = -0.57, p = 0.010, n = 19). Following adjustment for age and disease duration, associations between stress and fibromyalgia impact, central sensitization, and current and worst pain intensity, together with associations between pro-inflammatory diet and IL-6 and IL-10, and between BMI and IL-10 showed similar directions and effect estimates. However, following FDR adjustment as a sensitivity analysis, no associations retained statistical significance. Conclusions: This study suggests that different modifiable lifestyle factors may be associated with distinct aspects of pain and inflammatory processes in women with fibromyalgia. Perceived stress showed the most consistent associations with pain-related outcomes, while dietary inflammatory potential showed preliminary associations with inflammatory biomarkers that need further investigation.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythm-Related Characteristics and Adiposity in Relation to CAP-Defined Hepatic Steatosis Among Shift and Non-Shift Workers: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is the most prevalent chronic liver disease worldwide and linked to shift work. This study aimed to investigate the associations of circadian rhythm, sleep characteristics, anthropometric measures, and adiposity-related parameters with controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) values, and to assess their independent associations and sex-specific discriminatory performance in identifying hepatic steatosis among shift and non-shift workers. Methods: A total of 436 workers (328 men and 108 women), aged 19-64 years, from seven large-scale tea factories in Rize, Türkiye, were included. Social jetlag (SJL) and eating jetlag (EJL) were calculated from workday-free-day differences in sleep and meal timing, respectively, and sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Multivariable linear regression and sex-specific receiver operating characteristic analyses were performed. Results: Mean SJL (p = 0.017) and the distribution of SJL categories (p = 0.022) differed significantly between female shift and non-shift workers, whereas neither differed in men (p = 0.827 and p = 0.542, respectively). These comparisons are exploratory because SJL and EJL estimates are not directly comparable across rotating shift assignments or between shift and non-shift workers. CAP values and the prevalence of CAP-defined hepatic steatosis did not differ significantly by shift-work status in either sex. CAP was positively correlated with anthropometric and adiposity-related measures, with the strongest adjusted correlations observed for waist circumference, abdominal volume index (AVI), BMI, and body fat mass (all rs = 0.66, p < 0.001). In the fully adjusted regression model, age, BMI, and neck circumference were independently associated with higher CAP values, whereas SJL, EJL, sleep duration, and PSQI total score were not. In sex-specific ROC analyses, waist circumference and AVI showed the highest discriminatory performance in men (both AUC = 0.86), whereas BMI showed the highest discriminatory performance in women (AUC = 0.81). SJL and EJL did not significantly discriminate hepatic steatosis in either sex, while sleep duration showed weak discrimination in women (AUC = 0.63, q = 0.042). Conclusions: Anthropometric and adiposity-related measures were strongly associated with CAP values and showed good sex-specific discriminatory performance for hepatic steatosis. However, SJL findings, particularly comparisons by shift-work status, should be considered exploratory given the limited comparability of SJL and EJL estimates among rotating shift workers and between shift and non-shift workers. These simple, readily obtainable anthropometric measurements and derived adiposity indices may facilitate preliminary risk stratification for hepatic steatosis in occupational settings.

papers.title: Independent and Joint Associations of Diet Quality and Rest-Activity Rhythm Phenotypes with Frailty Among Rural Older Adults.
papers.abstract: Objectives: This study aimed to identify rest-activity rhythm (RAR) phenotypes and examine the independent and joint associations of RAR phenotypes and diet quality with frailty among rural older adults. Methods: This cross-sectional study included 1203 rural Chinese adults aged 65 to 85 years. Accelerometer-derived inter-daily stability, intra-daily variability, and relative amplitude were used to identify RAR phenotypes through latent profile analysis. Diet quality was assessed using the China Prime Diet Quality Score, and frailty was assessed using the Fried Frailty Phenotype. RAR phenotypes and median-dichotomized diet quality were combined into joint groups. Robust linear and ordered logistic regression examined associations with frailty score and severity, respectively. Subgroup and interaction analyses were conducted by sex and age group. Results: Five RAR phenotypes were identified. Compared with the robust-rhythm phenotype, the severely disrupted phenotype was associated with a 0.516-point higher frailty score and 148.6% higher odds of greater frailty severity, while the fragmented low-amplitude phenotype was associated with 49.3% higher odds. Each 10-point increase in diet quality score was associated with a 0.127-point lower frailty score and 29.3% lower odds of greater frailty severity. Joint analyses showed greater frailty in both typical-rhythm and fragmented low-amplitude phenotypes combined with lower diet quality (β = 0.229, OR = 2.020; β = 0.250, OR = 2.179, respectively), with the highest frailty score observed in the severely disrupted and lower-diet-quality group (β = 0.600; OR = 2.774). Severely disrupted combinations were associated with greater frailty whether diet quality was higher (β = 0.512; OR = 3.092) or lower (β = 0.600; OR = 2.774). No evidence of overall interaction by sex or age group was observed. Conclusions: Better diet quality and more robust RAR patterns were independently associated with lower frailty. Considering both factors may provide a broader perspective on behavioral factors related to frailty in older adults.

papers.title: Efficacy of a Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 and BG-R46® Formulation in Predominantly Breastfed Infants with Infant Distress Syndrome: A Randomized Double-Blind Placebo-Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Background: Infant distress syndrome, previously termed Infantile colic, is a common disorder of gut-brain interaction characterized by excessive crying and impaired behavioral regulation. Although Limosilactobacillus reuteri DSM 17938 has shown efficacy in predominantly breastfed infants, treatment responses remain variable, highlighting the need to investigate alternative probiotic formulations. BG-R46™, a strain derived from DSM 17938, exhibits distinct properties in preclinical models, providing a rationale for evaluating the combined formulation. This study investigated the efficacy and tolerability of DSM 17938 plus BG-R46™ compared with placebo in infants with infantile colic. Methods: In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 50 infants were randomized to receive either the probiotic formulation or placebo for 21 days. Forty-eight infants (24 per group) were included in the intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses. The primary endpoint was the change from baseline to Day 7 in total infant distress time, defined as the sum of awake fussing, crying, and inconsolable crying recorded using the Baby's Day Diary®. Secondary outcomes included crying time, infant behavioral regulation (sleep duration, awake and content behavior, awake fussing, and inconsolable crying), maternal emotional well-being assessed using the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS), and safety. Results: Baseline infant distress time was comparable between groups. At Day 7, infant distress time decreased by 43% in the probiotic group versus 13% in the placebo group (-236.0 ± 111.5 vs. -66.7 ± 100.1 min/day; p < 0.001). At Day 21, reductions reached 62% and 26%, respectively. The probiotic formulation was well tolerated throughout the study. Conclusions: Supplementation with L. reuteri DSM 17938 plus L. reuteri BG-R46™ significantly reduced infant distress compared with placebo.

papers.title: A Variational Autoencoder Network for Heartbeat Signal Reconstruction and Breathing-State Classification Using 24 GHz Radar Sensors.
papers.abstract: Wireless radar sensors can remotely detect vital signs. This study investigates the wireless monitoring of physiological signals induced by respiration and heartbeat to classify breathing states. Two 24 GHz radar sensors are used. Noise, harmonics, and intermodulation products affect the measured physiological signals and can make heartbeat identification and analysis challenging. Deep-learning techniques have recently been used to denoise and classify signals in wireless communications. Variational autoencoders (VAEs) have also been used for signal and image processing. Multilayer VAEs support sequential learning by optimizing generative-model parameters and reducing reconstruction error. This study investigates the separation of measured heartbeat and respiratory signals and the reduction in noise and the effects of limited random body movements using VAEs under controlled conditions. Two radars are positioned in front of and behind a human subject to record vital signals simultaneously. The separated and denoised heartbeat signals are input to a ResNet network to classify normal and fast breathing states. The proposed method achieves 99.7% accuracy on the reported experimental dataset.

papers.title: Reproducible EEG-BCI Experiments: Frame-Confirmed Timing and Physical SSVEP Validation.
papers.abstract: Reproducible EEG-based brain-computer interface (BCI) experiments require traceability from the configured protocol through runtime execution to acquisition context and, where relevant, the physical stimulus delivered to the participant. This study presents and evaluates a workflow that links machine-readable SSVEP protocols, deterministic session planning, frame-confirmed events, raw acquisition provenance, post-session integrity checks, and independent photoresistor-based display validation. The contribution is not a new acquisition platform or timing sensor, but the integration of these evidence layers into a single auditable experimental chain and the empirical assessment of their consistency. All 61 automated tests passed for the frozen software release. Three optical sweeps covering 8-15 Hz yielded 48 valid measurements, all within the predefined ±0.25 Hz criterion. The mean absolute error was 0.0345 Hz, and the maximum was 0.0668 Hz. In a separate 12.75 Hz rendering-load experiment, all 12 measurements also passed, with mean absolute errors of 0.0170 Hz for a single stimulus and 0.0154 Hz with three simultaneous distractors. Local optical pulse-width anomalies were, nevertheless, observed, particularly at 13-14 Hz and in two multi-stimulus repetitions, showing that dominant-frequency agreement and local timing regularity are distinct validation properties. Formal empirical validation targeted software and session integrity and physical display output; it did not quantify end-to-end event-to-EEG latency through the OpenBCI transport path. The results support a more explicit separation of configured intent, runtime timing evidence, acquisition provenance, and physical stimulus verification in reproducible EEG-BCI experimentation.

papers.title: Technical Feasibility of Respiratory Monitoring in Dogs Using Time-of-Flight Depth Imaging.
papers.abstract: Time-of-flight (ToF) depth imaging offers contactless observation of respiratory surface motion in veterinary patients. We investigated the technical feasibility of extracting canine respiratory waveforms and explored agreement between recorded camera-derived respiratory rates and concurrent manual counts. Depth images were acquired at a nominal 10 frames/s, and a fixed region of interest (ROI) supplied a mean depth signal. Clinical rates were obtained using Fourier spectral analysis with interpolation. Four dogs contributed eight sessions and 40 paired one-minute observations. Mean bias was +2.33 breaths/min (95% confidence interval -3.60 to +8.25), mean absolute error was 3.93 breaths/min, and exploratory repeated-measures limits of agreement were -10.40 to +15.05 breaths/min. One dog accounted for 69.4% of the absolute error and all observations above 25 breaths/min. Supplementary analyses compared spectral and peak-based estimates on identical inputs. An additional analysis of 27 ROI configurations in each of two recordings from one dog found maximum minute estimate changes of 7.50 and 7.80 breaths/min relative to a fixed baseline ROI. These findings demonstrate waveform extraction and dependence on spatial and temporal processing. They do not establish reliable respiratory rate measurement across dogs or respiratory rate ranges. The small independent sample, heterogeneous errors, incomplete original FFT configuration records and unquantified reference timing constrain the clinical comparison.

papers.title: EEG Biomarkers for Stress Detection: A Comparative Analysis of Hjorth Parameters, Spectral and Fractal-Dimension Measures.
papers.abstract: EEG-based stress detection is increasingly relevant for intelligent sensing and human-computer interaction, particularly for systems that aim to adapt to users' changing cognitive and affective states. While conventional EEG-based stress detection approaches mainly rely on spectral band-power features, fractal-dimension measures and Hjorth parameters may provide additional information about underlying brain dynamics. However, their relative contribution, spatial distribution, and frequency-band dependence remain insufficiently understood. In this study, pre-recorded EEG data from a stress-inducing experiment were analyzed using statistical feature pre-selection and multiple machine-learning classifiers. The contribution of different EEG features was evaluated across participants, while scalp topographical maps were used to characterize the spatial distribution of informative features. The results identify Hjorth activity, frontal β asymmetry, and the γ/θ ratio as among the most frequently selected features in the ANOVA-based feature-selection analysis. Combined feature-space configurations including Hjorth parameters and fractal-dimension measures achieved higher classification performance than the conventional-feature reference configuration. These findings provide further insight into the spatial and frequency-specific characteristics of EEG features associated with the investigated stress-inducing cognitive task and demonstrate the value of combining conventional spectral features with Hjorth parameters and fractal-dimension measures for physiological-state sensing. The proposed approach may support the development of computationally efficient EEG-based monitoring of stress-related cognitive states for intelligent and adaptive human-computer interaction, including neuroadaptive and context-aware systems.

papers.title: Investigation of Brain Performance in the Schizophrenia Spectrum Using EEG with Mental and Temporal Effort.
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia Spectrum Disorder, widely known as causing behavioral changes, deprives many professionals-who remain capable of working-their jobs. This study aimed to investigate the use of electroencephalography exam (EEG) combined with standardized mental effort sequence as a complementary tool for clinical diagnosis and to monitor the treatment response in individuals with schizophrenia and those who want to return to professional activities. EEG recordings were acquired before (IR_Initial Register) and after (FR_Final Register) the completion of a set of timed mental effort tasks in a group of 25 clinically stable individuals diagnosed with schizophrenia with positive symptoms and an 11-member healthy volunteer control group. Data from both groups were compared using temporal and spectral descriptors, and the results were analyzed statistically. The results revealed that, in the FR phase, the Vtotal parameter for the schizophrenia group was 7.89% lower, and the frequency parameter was 16.35% lower than in the healthy group. Notable differences were observed in the tolerance parameter for the duration of sustained cognitive effort: 57.9% of healthy volunteers sustained 100% of the effort duration, compared with 6.1% of volunteers with schizophrenia.
authors: Bernadete Márcia Voichcoski Franco da Rosa

papers.title: A Lightweight Hybrid-Attention Conformer for Affective State Recognition from Wearable EEG.
papers.abstract: Recognizing affective states from electroencephalography (EEG) is a core task in affective computing, with applications in mental health monitoring and public safety. Most existing approaches rely on handcrafted features or image-based transformations of EEG, while transformer models capture global context at high computational cost. This study proposes KimiFormer, an end-to-end hybrid-attention Conformer that classifies raw EEG directly. A hierarchical Spatio-Temporal Stemming (STS) module tokenizes the multichannel signal and learns inter-electrode relationships. Stacked Conformer blocks combine linear and full attention in a 3:1 ratio, reducing computational cost while preserving long-range modeling. The model was evaluated on the public EEG Violence Dataset, recorded with a 14-channel wearable headset from 14 participants viewing violent and neutral videos. Under record-wise leave-one-record-out cross-validation with nested selection of the training hyperparameters, KimiFormer achieved 95.5% accuracy (97.0% under 10-fold cross-validation). On the external DREAMER dataset, its subject-independent performance remained close to chance (balanced accuracy 52.7% for valence and 50.2% for arousal), as did that of two established raw-EEG models. Ablation showed the STS module to be essential (65% accuracy without it). With 3.2 M parameters, 1.51 GFLOPs and an inference latency of 15.64 ms per sample, KimiFormer is suited to real-time, on-device processing of low-channel wearable EEG.

papers.title: Sensor-Based Assessment of Trunk-Lower Limb Neuromuscular Coordination During Flat Tennis Serve Using Surface Electromyography and Time-Frequency Intermuscular Coherence Analysis.
papers.abstract: To compare flat-serve performance, muscle activation, and trunk-lower limb time-frequency intermuscular coherence between professional and amateur tennis players. Twenty-four tennis players (17 male and 7 female), including 12 professional and 12 amateur players, participated in this cross-sectional group-comparison study. Each participant completed 10 valid flat serves under standardized testing conditions, and serve-placement accuracy was assessed using a predefined target area. Surface electromyographic signals from 10 dominant-side trunk and lower-limb muscles were recorded using a Delsys Trigno Wireless EMG System, while serve movements were captured using a Photron FASTCAM Mini AX200 high-speed camera. Electromyographic and video data were synchronized using a transistor-transistor logic trigger. Integrated electromyography (IEMG) was normalized to maximal voluntary contraction, and time-frequency intermuscular coherence was calculated for 21 trunk-lower limb muscle pairs across the α, β, and γ frequency bands. Between-group differences were examined using two-tailed independent-samples t-tests. The Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (BH-FDR) procedure was applied to outcome families involving multiple comparisons, with statistical significance determined at FDR q < 0.05. Serve-placement accuracy was significantly higher in the professional group than in the amateur group (69.2 ± 7.4% vs. 48.3 ± 8.9%; t = 6.26, raw p < 0.001, Cohen's d = 2.55). After BH-FDR correction, professional players showed significantly higher IEMG values in the soleus (t = 3.12, raw p = 0.005, FDR q = 0.019, d = 1.27), vastus medialis (t = 2.92, raw p = 0.008, FDR q = 0.020, d = 1.19), vastus lateralis (t = 2.60, raw p = 0.016, FDR q = 0.027, d = 1.06), gluteus maximus (t = 3.17, raw p = 0.004, FDR q = 0.019, d = 1.29), and latissimus dorsi (t = 2.74, raw p = 0.012, FDR q = 0.024, d = 1.12), but significantly lower IEMG in the rectus abdominis (t = -3.07, raw p = 0.006, FDR q = 0.019, d = -1.25). Several muscle pair-frequency combinations showed nominal differences based on raw p-values and moderate-to-large effect sizes; however, none of the time-frequency intermuscular coherence comparisons remained statistically significant after BH-FDR correction (all FDR q > 0.05). Professional players demonstrated greater flat-serve placement accuracy and a distinct distribution of trunk and lower-limb muscle activation. The coherence findings were exploratory and did not conclusively establish skill-level differences in trunk-lower limb intermuscular coupling. Flat-serve training may emphasize lower-limb support and propulsion, hip extension, and trunk stabilization rather than focusing exclusively on arm or racket actions.

papers.title: Multimodal Performance Prediction in Online Learning Using Bi-LSTM and Mixture of Experts.
papers.abstract: Educational records alone may not capture changes in students' classroom affective states. This study proposes Bi-LSTM-SCPM, a student comprehensive performance model (SCPM) integrating bidirectional long short-term memory (Bi-LSTM) with mixture of experts (MoE) regression. The dataset comprised 14,645 facial images from 71 students across three stages of 12-week computer-assisted translation courses. ResNet50 achieved 93.8% accuracy in positive-negative facial state classification. Bi-LSTM integrated stage scores derived from instructor-designated key periods and Bayesian smoothing into a student-level affective score (ZHCJ). ZHCJ was combined with educational information and prerequisite course performance to predict final grades. Across 30 matched student-level splits, MoE achieved an R2 of 0.943 ± 0.002 and an MAE of 1.144 ± 0.128 points, compared with 0.927 ± 0.002 and 1.274 ± 0.149 points for XGBoost. Both differences remained significant after Holm adjustment (p < 0.001). ZHCJ also outperformed summary statistics and direct stage score inputs under both predictors. The setting ϖ = 2 and k = 20 performed best within the nine-setting grid. These findings support the predictive value of integrating temporal affective representations and educational information within the study cohort.

papers.title: MM-SleepNet: An Automatic Sleep Staging Network Based on Modal Re-Weighting and Mamba.
papers.abstract: Sleep staging is the key step in sleep quality assessment and sleep disorder diagnosis. In clinical practice, doctors usually use polysomnography (PSG) to stage sleep. PSG contains physiological signals such as electroencephalography (EEG) and electrooculography (EOG) and is divided into continuous epochs of fixed duration. In order to achieve more efficient and accurate automatic interpretation of PSG, this paper proposes MM-SleepNet, an automatic sleep staging network based on modal re-weighting and Mamba. MM-SleepNet divides each epoch into several overlapping patches and uses a newly designed patch feature extractor to extract the features of each patch, in order to solve the problem of key waveforms in the patch being obscured by non-key waveforms throughout the epoch. Afterward, MM-SleepNet calculates the importance of different signals on patches at the same time point through a dynamic re-weighting module. MM-SleepNet uses a bidirectional Mamba encoder that considers positional encoding to learn contextual information across epochs to adapt to the transition patterns between sleep stages. The experimental results on the Sleep-EDF and ISRUC datasets show that the proposed MM-SleepNet outperforms state-of-the-art methods. In addition, ablation experiments have demonstrated the effectiveness of various modules in MM-SleepNet.

papers.title: EEG-Based Recognition of Self-Imagined Emotions Using Multi-Domain Features and Subject-Specific Calibration.
papers.abstract: Self-imagined emotional imagery, in which individuals internally generate emotional states without external induction, plays a key role in shaping affective brain-computer interface (BCI) systems. Robust generalization across individuals is challenging due to significant variability in EEG patterns. This study evaluates a multi-domain electroencephalography (EEG) decoding framework for self-imagined emotion recognition, integrating time-frequency features, functional connectivity, effective connectivity, and subject-specific calibration. EEG data were collected from 38 participants and categorized into four emotional conditions using the valence-arousal model. Time-frequency features were extracted using the wavelet transform; functional connectivity was assessed using the phase locking value (PLV) and Pearson's correlation; and effective connectivity was estimated using Granger causality. For comparison, a two-dimensional convolutional neural network (CNN) based on the continuous wavelet transform was implemented. Under pooled sample-wise cross-validation, PLV-based features combined with a support vector machine (SVM) achieved 97.0% accuracy, while the CNN reached 94.75%. Under leave-one-subject-out evaluation, accuracy declined to approximately 25-30%, indicating limited generalization to unseen participants. With subject-specific calibration using 75% of the target participant's data, the SVM achieved 95.0% accuracy. The results support the recognition of four emotional conditions under the evaluated protocol when data from the target participant are available. However, cross-subject generalizability remains a significant limitation. As the study was conducted under controlled experimental conditions, further research involving independent populations and experimental settings is necessary to evaluate the framework's robustness and applicability.

papers.title: Quantum-Kernel Learning for Subject-Independent EEG Emotion Recognition with Spectral-Connectivity Features.
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG)-based emotion recognition remains challenging under subject-independent evaluation because of substantial inter-subject variability. This study investigates the feasibility of state-fidelity-based quantum-kernel learning for subject-independent valence and arousal recognition using differential entropy (DE) and phase-locking value (PLV) features. Using the DEAP dataset, DE and PLV features were extracted and evaluated individually and in combination, with subject-wise normalization and F-score feature selection applied within the evaluation framework. Six features were retained for valence and eight for arousal. The selected features were encoded using a Qiskit ZFeatureMap, and the fidelity-based quantum kernel was evaluated through statevector simulation on a classical computer. Quantum-kernel, Linear, and RBF SVMs were compared using nested participant-grouped cross-validation across DE, PLV, and DE-PLV feature representations. For valence, the quantum-kernel SVM using DE features achieved the highest mean balanced accuracy of 59.18%. For arousal, the Linear SVM using DE features achieved the highest mean balanced accuracy of 54.16%. Overall, the three classifiers showed comparable performance across the evaluated feature representations. These results support the feasibility of state-fidelity-based quantum similarity for subject-independent EEG emotion recognition.

papers.title: Interrupted-Sampling Repeater Jamming Suppression for Frequency-Agile Radar Based on Time-Frequency Analysis and Multi-Domain Filtering.
papers.abstract: Interrupted-sampling repeater jamming (ISRJ) produces coherent false targets after pulse compression and degrades the reliability of frequency-agile radar sensors, particularly at low signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) and high jamming-to-signal ratio (JSR). Existing single-domain suppression methods often provide insufficient separation between jamming and target echoes and may attenuate target-bearing components. This paper proposes a joint time-frequency analysis and multi-domain filtering method for radar waveforms employing intra-pulse and inter-pulse frequency agility. A forwarded jamming segment retains the carrier frequency of the sampled sub-pulse while overlapping a subsequent sub-pulse with a different carrier frequency, producing a joint displacement in time and frequency relative to the genuine target echo. Based on this property, a sub-pulse-wise two-dimensional feature extraction strategy is developed in the short-time Fourier transform (STFT) domain. Empirical probability density criteria are derived from projections along the time and frequency axes to determine adaptive rejection thresholds. The resulting time-selective and frequency-selective rejection regions are combined through logical intersection to construct a two-dimensional notch filter. The retained components are reconstructed using the inverse STFT and processed by segmented pulse compression. Simulations covering direct, periodic, and cyclic ISRJ show that the proposed method suppresses coherent false targets while limiting the loss of pulse-compression gain. It achieves higher peak signal-to-jamming-plus-noise ratios than the reference method over the tested SNR and JSR ranges and remains effective under adverse conditions. The proposed method improves the interference resilience of frequency-agile radar sensors and provides more reliable target echoes for subsequent detection and parameter estimation.

papers.title: Sensor-Based Hand and Upper-Limb Movement Intention Recognition in Post-Stroke Rehabilitation: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: Sensor-based systems increasingly allow post-stroke rehabilitation devices to infer voluntary movement intention and respond to active effort, but approaches vary widely in sensor modality, target movement, recognition method, and application. This review mapped sensor-based hand and upper-limb intention recognition after stroke. Following the Population-Concept-Context framework and PRISMA-ScR, PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, MEDLINE, and PEDro were searched from inception to 21 July 2026, and IEEE Xplore was additionally searched on 24 September 2026. Studies using sensor-based systems to classify, decode, trigger, assess, or provide feedback on voluntary hand or upper-limb movement in adults with stroke were included and narratively synthesized. Of 1576 records, 17 studies were eligible: 5 electromyography (EMG)-based or myoelectric systems, 7 electroencephalography (EEG)/brain-computer interface (BCI)-based systems, 2 EMG-triggered functional electrical stimulation (FES) systems, and 3 multimodal assessment or feedback systems. Target movements were mainly hand opening/closing, grasping, and finger, wrist, or reaching movements. Applications ranged from intention-related physiological assessment and movement/performance feedback to real-time closed-loop control of robots, orthoses, exoskeletons, and FES. True multimodal sensor fusion was uncommon. Sensor-based intention-responsive rehabilitation after stroke has developed mainly through parallel EMG-based and EEG/BCI-based approaches, with limited multimodal integration and no standardized framework. The present review distinguishes direct intention decoding, sensor-triggered control, movement/performance feedback, and intention-related physiological assessment; future work should apply these distinctions consistently and advance multimodal integration and clinical validation.

papers.title: The Case for Low-Friction High-Adherence Passive Sleep-Tracking Devices in Longitudinal Monitoring of Neurodegenerative Disease.
papers.abstract: Digital health technologies are playing an increasingly important role in patient monitoring, able to capture longitudinal data to supplement scheduled episodic evaluations conducted by clinicians. Rapid advances in sensors and data processing algorithms have resulted in some highly sophisticated systems capable of monitoring and tracking numerous symptoms with high levels of sensitivity and specificity. These approaches, however, often require active engagement with the patient, potentially increasing burden in a clinical trial and often resulting in diminishing adherence over time. In the case of slow-progressing neurodegenerative diseases, this may become an obstacle, as often very subtle changes in symptoms are typically monitored over a multi-year period. Accordingly, there is evident interest in passive monitoring solutions which have minimal burden on patients. Smart ring technologies are one such solution, with appealing form factors, low engagement requirements and increasing intervals before device recharging is required. While newer devices are capable of tracking sleep function with increasing levels of accuracy, they are unable to offer the precision afforded by gold standard sleep analysis such as electroencephalography (EEG), polysomnography (PSG) and sleep laboratory protocols. Prompted by a recent study which highlighted the reduced accuracy of consumer-based sleep devices compared with conventional approaches, we posit that the benefits of such devices may offset the constraints of measurement accuracy. Furthermore, any accuracy-adherence trade-offs would be compensated by long-term statistical benefits derived from detecting within-person changes and reducing measurement noise through enhanced sampling frequencies. In this perspective, we highlight their potential utility in tracking Parkinson's disease patients longitudinally, where compromised sleep architectures are associated with multiple symptoms and continuous monitoring could offer myriad patient benefits.

papers.title: From COP1 Cofactors to Candidate Signaling Hubs: Emerging Roles of SPA Proteins in Plant Growth and Environmental Responses.
papers.abstract: SUPPRESSOR OF PHYA-105 (SPA) proteins bind the E3 ubiquitin ligase CONSTITUTIVELY PHOTOMORPHOGENIC 1 (COP1) and, within the COP1/SPA complex, repress light signaling in plants. For two decades, SPA proteins were regarded mainly as COP1 cofactors. Since 2019, Huq and colleagues have reported that recombinant SPA1 phosphorylates PHYTOCHROME INTERACTING FACTOR 1 (PIF1), PIF4, ELONGATED HYPOCOTYL 5 (HY5) and eukaryotic translation initiation factor 2α (eIF2α) in vitro. Here, we review the SPA family, from its evolution and domain architecture to its regulation by phytochromes, cryptochromes and UVR8, and we grade the evidence for each proposed function as established, reported, inferred or hypothetical. We separate in vitro phosphorylation from in vivo SPA dependence and catalytic validation, and SPA-specific genetic evidence from inferences based on COP1 or HY5. We then relate these mechanisms to de-etiolation, shade avoidance, thermomorphogenesis, photoperiodic flowering, circadian timing and anthocyanin accumulation, and we assess soybean SPA-like alleles that shorten internodes and have been associated with higher yield under dense planting in field trials. We propose, as a working hypothesis, that the SPA subunit is the signal-integrating module of the COP1/SPA complex, and we identify the experiments needed to test this model.

papers.title: Facility-Based Yoga for Adult Cancer Patients and Survivors at a National Cancer Institute (NCI)-Designated Comprehensive Cancer Center: A Retrospective Study of Program Utilization and Barriers to Care.
papers.abstract: Yoga is associated with improvements in quality of life and symptom burden in patients with cancer, yet barriers to participation persist. This study retrospectively evaluated real-world utilization, factors associated with attendance, symptom trajectories, and satisfaction with a yoga program at an NCI-designated comprehensive cancer center. Adults with a primary cancer diagnosis enrolled in the Integrative Oncology and Survivorship Program (January 2024-February 2026) who attended ≥1 yoga session were included. Patients attended weekly 60 min instructor-led classes. Attendance trends, baseline predictors of attendance, pre/post PROMIS-29 changes after four visits, and satisfaction ratings were analyzed using chi-square, rank-sum, and multivariable negative binomial regression. Among 148 patients, 80 (54.1%) attended ≥4 visits. Median age was 60 years; 44.6% identified as Black/African American. Attendance increased over time (70.1% in 2024 to 75.0% in early 2026). Patients aged ≥60 demonstrated 1.74-fold (IRR 1.74, 95%CI 1.05-2.90, p = 0.033)-higher attendance, while mild sleep disturbance was associated with lower attendance (IRR 0.26, 95%CI 0.09-0.74, p = 0.012). No significant PROMIS-29 domain changes were observed after four visits, though descriptive improvements were noted. Satisfaction was uniformly high; 93.8% rated likelihood of recommending the service as "Very Good". In this retrospective real-world study, facility-based yoga was well accepted and demonstrated improving utilization across a racially diverse oncology cohort. Older age was associated with greater engagement, while sleep disturbances may represent a barrier to sustained participation. and demonstrated improving utilization across a racially diverse oncology cohort. Older age was associated with greater engagement, while sleep disturbances may represent a barrier to sustained participation.

papers.title: Sleep Quality, Psychological Inflexibility, and Work-Private-Life Interference in Relation to Emotional Exhaustion Among Ecuadorian Nursing Assistants: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Evidence concerning emotional exhaustion among nursing assistants in Ecuador remains limited. This exploratory cross-sectional study examined associations of sleep quality, psychological inflexibility, and study-specific work-private-life interference with emotional exhaustion. The focus on emotional exhaustion as the sole outcome was selected during manuscript revision and was not prospectively prespecified. This analysis included 314 nursing assistants recruited through convenience sampling; 290 had calculable Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) scores and contributed to PSQI-dependent regression models. Emotional exhaustion was assessed using the nine-item Maslach Burnout Inventory subscale, psychological inflexibility using the AAQ-II, and work-private-life interference using three study-specific binary items. Ordinary least squares regression with HC3 heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors was evaluated using Python (statsmodels). Of 290 participants with valid PSQI scores, 144 (49.7%) had scores above five. In the main model (R2 = 0.432), poorer sleep quality (B = 0.915, 95% CI 0.599-1.231), higher AAQ-II scores (B = 0.196, 95% CI 0.054-0.338), and greater work-private-life interference (B = 3.386, 95% CI 2.454-4.317) were associated with higher emotional exhaustion. Associations persisted after adjustment for age, sex, and shift work. In an exploratory model additionally accounting for concurrent depression, anxiety, and stress symptoms, the AAQ-II association was no longer statistically significant (B = 0.058, p = 0.400). Sleep quality and study-specific work-private-life interference were consistently associated with emotional exhaustion. The cross-sectional design, non-probability sampling, and exploratory analyses preclude causal or population-level inferences.

papers.title: Low Muscle Mass, Sleep Quality, and Quality of Life Among Older Chinese Adults: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Background: Low muscle mass (LMM), poor sleep quality, and reduced quality of life (QOL) are common concerns in older adults. This study examined their cross-sectional associations and explored the statistical indirect association involving sleep quality, with particular attention to sensitivity to body-size adjustment and alternative model specifications. Methods: We analyzed data from 9366 adults aged 65 years or older in the 2018 Chinese Longitudinal Healthy Longevity Survey. LMM was classified using anthropometrically predicted appendicular skeletal muscle mass, while sleep quality and overall QOL were assessed using single-item self-reports. Regression-based indirect associations were estimated with 5000 bootstrap resamples. Sensitivity analyses examined alternative measurements, body-size adjustment, depressive symptoms, model ordering, missing-data assumptions, and sampling weights. Results: Anthropometrically estimated LMM was associated with poorer sleep quality (B = -0.066, 95% CI: -0.110 to -0.022) and lower QOL (total association: B = -0.073, 95% CI: -0.108 to -0.039). Better sleep quality was associated with higher QOL (B = 0.163, 95% CI: 0.147 to 0.178). The indirect association was small (B = -0.011, 95% bootstrap CI: -0.018 to -0.003) and attenuated after continuous body mass index adjustment (B = -0.001, 95% bootstrap CI: -0.010 to 0.008). Adjustment for depressive symptoms further attenuated the estimated indirect association, while a reverse-order model also yielded a non-zero indirect association (B = -0.020). Residual-confounding sensitivity analyses indicated dependence on assumptions about unmeasured common causes. Conclusions: Anthropometrically estimated LMM was associated with poorer perceived sleep quality and overall QOL, but the estimated indirect association involving sleep quality was small and sensitive to body-size adjustment, psychological covariates, and model specification. These cross-sectional findings do not establish a muscle-specific association independent of overall body size or a causal sleep-mediated pathway. Longitudinal studies incorporating directly measured body composition and validated multidimensional sleep and QOL assessments are needed to clarify these relationships.

papers.title: Loneliness and Mental Health Risks of Older People Living Alone in the Community: Cross-Sectional Study Protocol.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Some available evidence indicates an exponential rise regarding the proportion of older adults residing alone worldwide, which is associated with potential health and social risks, particularly those linked to loneliness and other mental health risk factors. This research aims to: (i) describe the physical and mental health profile of older people (aged over 65 years) living alone in the community, (ii) to examine the associations among the variables encompassing their mental health profile, and (iii) to explore the association between mental health and sociodemographic and health characteristics of this population. Methods: A cross-sectional study will be carried out. Potential participants must live alone in the selected municipality and be aged 65 years or older. Participants will be recruited through convenience sampling. Eleven instruments will be administered to participants assessing sociodemographic and health characteristics; fear of falling; sleep quality; frailty; anxiety, depression, and stress; loneliness; cognitive status; emotional literacy; perceived hope; functionality; and perceived social support. Data will be analysed using descriptive, univariate, and bivariate statistical methods. The study and its protocol were reviewed and approved by the Ethics Committee of a major public university in Northern Portugal (CEICVS 067/2022). Expected Results: This study aims to assess the physical and mental health of older adults living alone in a selected municipality in Northern Portugal, an area where such comprehensive data remain scarce. By conducting this analysis, we intend to inform and support the development of a highly personalized, evidence-based action plan, ultimately contributing to the mitigation of mental risk factors in this population.
authors: Maria do Perpétuo S S Nóbrega

papers.title: Nature, Characteristics, and Reported Experiences of Medical Malpractice Disputes Among Egyptian Physicians Practicing in Egypt and Other Arab Countries: A Cross-Sectional Medicolegal Analysis of Psychological Distress, Somatic Symptoms, and Defensive Behavior.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Medical malpractice disputes may affect physicians' well-being and clinical behavior. This study characterizes the medicolegal profile of malpractice disputes among Egyptian physicians practicing in Egypt and other Arab countries and examines how these disputes correlate with concurrent psychological, somatic, and defensive behavioral burdens. Methods: A cross-sectional online survey with nonprobability sampling was conducted from March to December 2025 among 586 practicing Egyptian physicians involved in at least one malpractice dispute. Participants completed the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale-6, the Impact of Event Scale-6, twelve items of the Defensive Medicine Behavior Scale, two items of the Malpractice Fear Scale, and a self-reported somatic symptom checklist. Multivariable regression identified independent correlates. Results: A lawsuit was the most serious dispute type for 51.4% of physicians, and management-related allegations were the most common (59.4%). Practice in Egypt rather than another Arab country was associated with procedure-related allegations (adjusted odds ratio 2.27; 95% confidence interval 1.49-3.45). Among resolved disputes, formal complaints (0.30; 0.18-0.49) and threats (0.45; 0.23-0.90) were less likely than lawsuits to end unfavorably for the physician. Recalling the dispute period, 62.3% had Kessler distress scores of 13 or more (mean 15.5 ± 6.4), with frequent post-traumatic stress symptoms (mean item score 2.7 ± 0.9) and somatic symptoms led by sleep disturbance (81.2%). High or very high defensive medicine scores were found in 92.0%. Conclusions: In this self-selected sample, malpractice disputes were associated with a heavy psychological, somatic, and behavioral burden. Medicolegal education, clearer complaint pathways, better documentation systems, and visible institutional peer support are policy considerations that need prospective evaluation.

papers.title: Shift Work and Acute Coronary Syndrome: Mechanisms, Modifying Factors, and Clinical Prevention.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Shift work causes recurrent circadian misalignment. This review synthesizes evidence linking shift work to acute coronary syndrome (ACS) and proposes a framework for prevention, return-to-work decisions, and future research. Methods: We conducted a narrative review using targeted searches of PubMed and major guideline repositories through July 2026. Search terms included shift work, night work, acute coronary syndrome, myocardial infarction, coronary heart disease, circadian misalignment, sleep, thrombosis, and cardiovascular risk. Revision-stage verification also examined atherosclerosis, coronary plaque, plaque vulnerability, and ischemia. Priority was given to prospective cohorts, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, controlled human studies, consensus statements, and major guidelines. Results: Night and rotating shift work are associated with a modestly increased risk of coronary heart disease (relative risk ~1.2-1.3), with duration-response gradients. Direct ACS-specific evidence is more limited but consistent with increased incidence and recurrence. Mechanistically, circadian misalignment and sleep deficiency promote autonomic dysregulation, hypertension, insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and atherosclerosis. Acute autonomic, hemodynamic, and prothrombotic changes may trigger plaque disruption or supply-demand ischemia. Risk modifiers include schedule intensity, cumulative exposure, chronotype, age, sex, comorbidities, sleep disorders, occupation, and health behaviors. Pregnancy is a specific evidence gap. Conclusions: Night and rotating shift work are probable contributory risk factors for ACS in susceptible workers. Clinical practice should integrate work schedule and sleep health into cardiovascular assessment, especially after ACS. Roster redesign offers the most defensible preventive strategy. Evidence that circadian interventions prevent ACS remains insufficient. More prospective ACS-specific studies are needed.

papers.title: Associations of Ultra-Processed Food Intake with Body Composition and Blood Pressure Across Sasang Constitution Types: A Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: High ultra-processed food (UPF) consumption is linked to adverse health outcomes. In Koreans, UPFs contribute approximately one-quarter of daily energy intake. We examined whether the longitudinal associations between UPF intake and changes in body composition, blood pressure (BP), and sleep parameters differ across Sasang constitution types (Taeum, Soeum, and Soyang). This prospective cohort study included 182 adults aged ≥30 years (baseline: 2015-2017; follow-up: 2019-2021). Dietary intake was assessed only at baseline using a 63-item food frequency questionnaire, and the percentage of total energy intake from UPFs (%UPF) was calculated. Multivariable linear regression models with baseline adjustment were used to evaluate longitudinal changes and interaction effects. In the Soeum type, higher %UPF intake was significantly associated with progressive longitudinal increases in weight (β = 0.27 kg, 95% CI: 0.08 to 0.46), and body mass index (β = 0.09 kg/m2, 95% CI: 0.02 to 0.16), and body fat mass (β = 0.15 kg, 95% CI: 0.00 to 0.30) per 1% increment in %UPF intake, with significant linear dose-response trends across tertiles observed only for weight and BMI (p for trend < 0.05). In the Soyang type, continuous %UPF intake was positively associated with systolic BP (β = 0.36 mmHg, 95% CI: 0.01 to 0.70). No significant longitudinal associations were observed in the Taeum type or for sleep parameters. Overall interaction terms between %UPF intake and constitution types were not statistically significant (all p for interaction > 0.05). In constitution-stratified analyses, higher %UPF intake was longitudinally associated with adverse changes in body composition in the Soeum type and in blood pressure in the Soyang type. Although overall interactions were non-significant, considering constitutional traits alongside dietary assessments may provide exploratory insights into cardiometabolic risk prevention.

papers.title: Pregnancy-Recognized Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Maternal-Fetal Outcomes: A Narrative Review of Gestational Rhinitis, Upper-Airway Mechanisms, and Treatment Evidence.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Pregnancy-recognized obstructive sleep apnea (POSA) is an operational construct, not a validated biological phenotype, and remains underrecognized in prenatal care. This review synthesizes evidence on POSA-related outcomes, evaluates gestational rhinitis as a candidate contributor to upper-airway vulnerability, and distinguishes pregnancy safety from demonstrated efficacy for OSA-related endpoints. Methods: This structured narrative review, informed by SANRA criteria, used a structured PubMed search (7 March 2026) with targeted supplementary searches through 9 October 2026, across six predefined domains. Results: Pregnancy-recognized OSA is associated in observational studies with hypertensive disorders, preterm birth, impaired fetal growth (in small pregnancy-specific studies), and severe maternal morbidity; residual confounding by obesity precludes causal inference. In a 2024 meta-analysis of randomized and observational studies (n = 809), continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) was associated with lower risks of gestational hypertension (RR, 0.65; 95% CI, 0.47-0.89) and preeclampsia (RR, 0.70; 95% CI, 0.50-0.98). Although secondary endpoints in individual trials suggested benefit, the pooled preeclampsia effect was fragile in sensitivity and subgroup analyses. Gestational rhinitis affects approximately one in five pregnant women and is a plausible but untested contributor to pregnancy-recognized OSA. Saline irrigation, budesonide (mainly inhaled-exposure data), and chlorpheniramine have gestational safety data, but the only randomized trial of an intranasal corticosteroid in gestational rhinitis was null, and we identified no study of OSA endpoints. Conclusions: Given the largely observational evidence, objective testing and individualized treatment may be considered in high-risk patients, pending adequately powered trials. CPAP is the standard treatment for objectively confirmed OSA.

papers.title: From Risk to Resilience: A Narrative Synthesis of Protective Factors and Proposed Mechanisms in Bias-Based Bullying Among Youth (2016-2026).
papers.abstract: Bias-based bullying (BBB) is a public health concern associated with psychological distress, suicidality, school disengagement, and other adverse health and developmental outcomes. This review synthesized empirical evidence on protective factors and examined proposed mechanisms and contextual conditions associated with how they operate. A theory-informed narrative synthesis was conducted using empirical studies published from 2016 through 2026 identified through APA PsycInfo, APA PsycArticles, ERIC, PubMed, Web of Science, and supplementary searches. Fifty-nine studies met the inclusion criteria and were appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool. Findings were coded iteratively and interpreted through an integrated ecological and resource-based theoretical framework. Protective factors were identified across individual, interpersonal, and institutional levels. Individual strengths were more often associated with reduced harm than reduced exposure, whereas relational and institutional resources were more frequently associated with protective outcomes. Protective associations varied according to macro climate and policy context, intersecting identities and cumulative targeting, and proximal school and peer activation processes. No single factor was associated with protection for all youth, outcomes, or forms of BBB, and protective associations were often weaker under cumulative exposure. The findings suggest that protection depends on coordinated, accessible, and credible resources across ecological systems. Healthcare professionals should consider identity-based victimization when assessing youth with emotional distress, self-harm risk, disordered eating, sleep problems, or school disengagement, with attention to identity-responsive environments, accessible services, and coordinated follow-up.

papers.title: Multidimensional Frailty-Related Vulnerability Profiles Among Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Data-Driven Cluster Analysis of the 2023 National Survey of Older Koreans.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Frailty-related vulnerability spans health, physical function, health behaviors, cognition, and psychological well-being. A single summary score may not fully convey how these features co-occur within individuals. This study identified data-driven frailty-related profiles among community-dwelling older adults and compared the magnitude of between-profile differences. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of the 2023 National Survey of Older Koreans. The analytical sample included 9950 participants. Ten indicators-self-rated health, chronic disease count, 1-year weight loss, sleep quality, weekly exercise frequency, fatigue, stair-climbing ability, 300-m walking ability, cognitive function, and depressive symptoms-were standardized and entered into K-means clustering. Candidate solutions for K = 2-10 were evaluated using within-cluster sums of squares and mean silhouette coefficients. Profile characteristics and effect sizes were compared using independent-samples t-tests, Pearson's chi-squared tests, Cohen's d, and Cramér's V. Results: The K = 2 solution had the highest mean silhouette coefficient (0.273) among the candidate solutions, indicating modest separation between clusters. Within the analytical sample, 6962 participants (70.0%) formed a lower-vulnerability profile and 2988 (30.0%) a multidimensional higher-vulnerability profile. The latter profile showed less favorable health, functional, psychological, and cognitive characteristics. Among the cluster-defining indicators, the largest descriptive differences were observed in 300-m walking (d = 2.013) and stair-climbing ability (d = 2.001). Conclusions: The two clusters represented a relative multidimensional vulnerability gradient rather than clearly distinct clinical phenotypes. Although the findings describe co-occurring vulnerability characteristics, their potential clinical utility requires independent and longitudinal validation.

papers.title: Symptom Networks in Patients Receiving Dialysis: A Systematic Review of Node Centrality, Bridge Centrality, and Methodological Quality.
papers.abstract: Patients receiving dialysis experience multiple interacting physical and psychological symptoms. Network analysis can identify symptoms occupying central or bridging positions, but findings across dialysis studies have not been systematically synthesized. This review aimed to synthesize central and bridge symptoms in adults receiving dialysis and evaluate the methodological quality of symptom network studies. Following PRISMA 2020 and a prospectively registered protocol (PROSPERO CRD420261410561), PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, CINAHL, China National Knowledge Infrastructure, and Wanfang Data were searched from inception to 9 May 2026. Two reviewers independently screened studies and assessed methodological quality. Centrality rankings from studies using the Dialysis Symptom Index or modified versions were min-max normalized and synthesized. Sixteen cross-sectional studies involving 7691 participants were included; 15 were conducted in mainland China and one in Singapore, while 14 involved hemodialysis populations and two involved peritoneal dialysis populations. Nine network models contributed to the centrality-ranking synthesis. Anxiety ranked first (median normalized rank 0.0690), followed by difficulty falling asleep (0.2353) and sadness (0.2400). Fatigue and irritability were most frequently identified as bridge or connecting symptoms. Thirteen studies reported strength correlation-stability coefficients of at least 0.50. Seven studies were rated low quality, eight moderate quality, and one high quality, with recurrent deficiencies in model-selection reporting, subgroup comparisons, raw centrality values, and uncertainty assessment. Psychological and sleep-related symptoms occupied prominent positions in the analyzed networks, while fatigue frequently connected symptom communities. The evidence predominantly reflects hemodialysis samples from mainland China. The applicability to peritoneal dialysis populations and to other healthcare systems and cultural settings remains uncertain. These cross-sectional findings are hypothesis-generating and require validation in more diverse populations.

papers.title: Long Sleep Duration and Multimorbidity in Older U.S. Adults: A Dose-Response Analysis of NHANES 2017-March 2020.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Sleep disturbance and chronic-disease multimorbidity are both common in aging populations, yet the dose-response shape of their association in U.S. older adults, and the sleep threshold of clinical relevance, remain unclear. Methods: We analyzed 2998 community-dwelling U.S. adults aged ≥60 years from the NHANES 2017-March 2020 pre-pandemic cycle. Self-reported sleep duration was categorized as short (<6 h), normal (6-8 h), or long (>8 h); multimorbidity was ≥2 of eleven physician-diagnosed chronic conditions. Survey-weighted logistic regression with jackknife variance estimated adjusted odds ratios (aORs), and restricted cubic splines characterized the dose-response shape. Results: Multimorbidity prevalence was 64.0%. The excess risk was confined to sleep of ≥9 h (aOR = 1.65, 95% CI 1.22-2.25); the band immediately above the reference, >8 to <9 h, showed no elevation (aOR = 1.08, 0.67-1.73), and the spline was J-shaped (P-nonlinearity = 0.005). Across the conventional >8 h category, long sleep was associated with multimorbidity (aOR = 1.41, 1.08-1.85, p = 0.014), whereas short sleep was not (aOR = 0.92, 0.58-1.47). This corresponded to an adjusted risk difference of 7.0 percentage points, and it was not materially attenuated by adjustment for a frailty phenotype (aOR = 1.38, 1.00-1.90) or among participants carrying at most one of the three available frailty criteria (aOR = 1.42, 1.03-1.97). The E-value, corrected for this common outcome, was 1.51. Conclusions: Long sleep, particularly ≥9 h, was associated with multimorbidity along a J-shaped dose-response. The association was moderate and the cross-sectional design cannot exclude reverse causation, so long sleep is best interpreted as a marker of accumulated disease burden rather than an actionable risk factor.

papers.title: Twenty-Four-Hour Movement Behaviors and Adult Mental Health: A Bibliometric Analysis of Global Trends, Research Hotspots, and Emerging Directions (2016-2026).
papers.abstract: Physical activity, sedentary behavior, and sleep constitute interdependent components of the 24-hour day and are jointly associated with mental health in adults. This study aimed to examine the global research landscape, hotspots, and emerging trends in this field from 2016 to 2026. Records published between 1 January 2016,and 30 April 2026, were retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. The bibliometrix package (version 5.3.0), implemented in R (version 4.5.2), was used to analyze publication and citation trends and contributions from countries, institutions, authors, and journals. Country-level publication output was quantified using full counting of unique document-country pairs, such that each publication was counted only once for a given country, whereas internationally co-authored publications were credited to all participating countries. Country citation rankings were determined by aggregating citations according to the corresponding author's country of affiliation. VOSviewer (version 1.6.20) was used to construct country-level co-authorship networks using full counting and to generate keyword co-occurrence networks. The R packages ggplot2 and circlize were used for additional visualizations, including chord diagrams of citation relationships among journals. A total of 527 publications were included. The annual global production from 2016 to 2026 reflected an overall upward trend with significant fluctuations. The amount of global output peaked in 2024 with 147 publications, whereas the number of total citations reached its highest in 2022 (2702). The United States was involved in 152 of the included publications, China in 118, and Australia in 87. Australia recorded the highest total citations (1757), followed by the United States (1667) and China (1556). Keyword overlay visualization revealed a shift from traditional behavioral epidemiology focused on workplace behaviors and subjective well-being toward integrated, precision-oriented mental health research emphasizing aging, cognitive health, circadian rhythm, and objective behavioral monitoring. Emerging hotspots included machine learning, compositional data analysis, isotemporal substitution, and accelerometer-based assessment. Research on 24-hour movement behaviors and adult mental health has evolved into an increasingly interdisciplinary field, with growing emphasis on integrated behavioral approaches, objective assessment methods, and healthy aging.

papers.title: Cardiovascular Comorbidity in Obstructive Sleep Apnea: The "Excessive Daytime Sleepiness" Phenotype Versus Comorbid Insomnia and Sleep Apnea (COMISA).
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Excessive daytime sleepiness (EDS) and comorbid insomnia and sleep apnea (COMISA) are common clinical phenotypes of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). We compared their cardiovascular and metabolic comorbidity. Methods: Cross-sectional, single-center retrospective analysis of adults with polygraphy-confirmed OSA (apnea-hypopnea index ≥ 5 events/h). The EDS phenotype was defined as an Epworth Sleepiness Scale score ≥ 10 without insomnia (n = 54), and COMISA as OSA with clinically reported insomnia (n = 45). Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with phenotype. Results: OSA severity and the prevalence of any cardiovascular disease (90.7% vs. 86.7%) were similar. In the adjusted model, higher BMI (aOR 0.92 per kg/m2) and cardiac arrhythmias (aOR 0.20) were associated with lower odds of COMISA, and dyslipidemia with higher odds (aOR 2.51). Conclusions: Both phenotypes carry a high cardiovascular burden, but they seem to differ in metabolic profile: severe obesity and an arrhythmic tendency in sleepy OSA, and dyslipidemia in COMISA.

papers.title: Explainable Rhythm-Resolved EEG for Retrospective Comparison of Psychiatric-Service Adults with Recorded Violent Offences and Non-Clinical Controls.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: This study examines whether rhythm-resolved EEG features separate two retrospective groups and whether those features can be traced to explicit rhythms and sensors.
