papers.title: Beyond Set Points: Rhythm-Based Detection of Change in Honey Bee Colony State from Hive Sensor Data.
papers.abstract: Disruption of daily patterns of activity, physiology, or social interaction is associated with stress and reduced fitness across species. In social insects such as honey bees (Apis mellifera), circadian organisation extends to the colony level, where rhythms emerge from interactions among individual clocks, hive conditions, and environmental cues. Precision apiculture offers a mature sensor toolkit for measuring colony-level variables, and several data streams carry early-warning information about colony condition. Almost all alarms, however, are triggered against set points rather than against the daily rhythm of the signal. We review each sensor technology to establish whether its data have been, or could be, analysed with a chronobiological lens, describing the measurement principle, the achievable temporal resolution and record continuity, the rhythmic signature expected on biological grounds, and any evidence that such a signature has been reported. We then use a synthetic dataset to illustrate the workflow: in this simulated example, rhythm metrics flagged a gradually developing decline approximately three weeks before a conventional threshold alert on the same data. This lead time is a property of the simulation and awaits validation on real colonies. Wherever continuous behavioural monitoring is deployed, rhythm-based metrics may offer a route to earlier, more interpretable detection of change than set point comparisons.

papers.title: Ligand-Specific Remodeling of the Anopheles gambiae RDL GABA Receptor by the A296S Mutation Differentiates Recognition of Fipronil and Fluralaner.
papers.abstract: The γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA)-gated chloride channel Resistance to Dieldrin (RDL) receptor is a major molecular target of insecticides, yet the structural basis by which resistance-associated mutations differentially influence chemically distinct ligands remains incompletely understood. Here, we investigated the effects of the classical A296S substitution on the interactions of the Anopheles gambiae RDL receptor with the phenylpyrazole fipronil and the isoxazoline fluralaner using homology modeling, molecular docking, 200 ns molecular dynamics simulations (apo receptors and three independent replicas of each ligand-bound complex), and MM/PBSA free-energy calculations that include an interaction-entropy (IE) term. Apo-state molecular dynamics simulations showed that A296S preserved the overall structural stability of the receptor while locally modifying the environment of the pore-lining M2 transmembrane helix. Although docking scored fluralaner more favorably than fipronil in both receptor variants, the replicated molecular dynamics simulations revealed ligand- and genotype-dependent behavior. In the wild-type receptor, fluralaner remained stably bound and had a favorable MM/PBSA free-energy estimate (-18.3 ± 4.2 kcal/mol), whereas the ligand RMSD of fipronil increased progressively and its estimate was close to zero (+1.2 ± 9.5 kcal/mol). In the A296S model, the fipronil estimate was similar (+1.6 ± 4.3 kcal/mol), but the fluralaner estimate became unfavorable (+10.0 ± 1.8 kcal/mol), and Ser296 itself contributed slightly unfavorably to both ligands. Together, these findings indicate that A296S does not act as a universal determinant of ligand recognition but is associated with ligand-specific changes in the modeled interaction landscape, with the larger predicted effect on fluralaner. These predictions derive from a homology model, were not tested by electrophysiology or binding assays, and do not measure functional resistance. They may nonetheless help inform the interpretation of cross-resistance patterns and structure-guided efforts targeting GABA receptor-based insecticides.

papers.title: Regional Arboreal Pollen Input and Its Millennial-Scale Variability Recorded in an Alpine Lake in the Hengduan Mountains, China.
papers.abstract: The Hengduan Mountains are a major hotspot for lake-sediment research, but regional vegetation responses to Holocene climate variability remain incompletely understood. Here, we analyzed pollen assemblages and concentrations from Dinggongniang Co (4633 m a.s.l.) to investigate regional vegetation-related changes over the past approximately 4.7 ka. Pollen percentage and concentration analyses were combined with ensemble empirical mode decomposition (EEMD) and Lomb-Scargle spectral analysis. Despite being located above the modern tree line, the lake sediments are dominated by arboreal pollen (89.5%), particularly Pinus, indicating substantial pollen input from lower-elevation forests. Total pollen concentrations were relatively low around 4.2 ka, increased markedly during the Roman Warm Period, and remained relatively elevated during the Medieval Climate Anomaly, suggesting changes in regional arboreal pollen input potentially associated with Asian summer monsoon-related hydroclimatic variability. Furthermore, time-series analyses identified a possible millennial-scale oscillation at approximately 1.3-1.4 ka, broadly consistent with variability documented in North Atlantic and Asian monsoon records. This finding highlights the value of high-altitude lake pollen records for tracing regional arboreal pollen input and suggests possible connections between Asian monsoon variability and broader Northern Hemisphere climate fluctuations. Although chronological uncertainties and multiple factors influencing pollen concentrations introduce some limitations, the observed patterns offer valuable insights into long-term vegetation-related environmental variability in the Hengduan Mountains.

papers.title: Hemodynamic spectral signatures across vigilance states: a whole-night EEG/fNIRS investigation.
papers.abstract: Sleep is accompanied by coordinated changes in neuronal activity and cerebral hemodynamics. However, cortical hemodynamic signatures across sleep stages remain poorly characterized, partly because most human electroencephalography (EEG)/functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies are limited in duration, rarely capture deep or Rapid-Eye-Movement (REM) sleep, have low sampling rate, or rely on a sleep-deprivation paradigm, which limits the generalizability of findings. Here, we combined whole-night polysomnography, EEG and functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) in healthy young adults, as a bedside technology to monitor cortical hemodynamic fluctuations. We recorded fNIRS using an optimal, personalized, locally dense bilateral frontoparietal montage, alongside peripheral physiology recordings (respiration, photoplethysmography, mean arterial pressure). We computed oscillatory components of oxy- and deoxyhemoglobin (HbO-HbR) spectra across sleep stages using wavelet-based time-frequency analysis. Additionally, we analyzed within the same regions an independent sleep EEG-fMRI dataset (no REM recorded). Our results are suggesting that across frontal and parietal regions, slow-frequency (0.002-0.1Hz) power increased during N1 sleep in HbO and then progressively attenuated across N2 and N3 sleep, in HbO, HbR, and fMRI. REM showed a re-emergence of very-low-frequency power (<0.01Hz) in HbO and HbR. Higher-frequency oscillations (0.15-0.5Hz; overlapping respiratory-band) were selectively enhanced during NREM sleep (largest increase during N3) and returned toward wake-like levels during REM in frontal regions, with regional differences. Peripheral signals captured systemic physiology oscillations but did not reproduce the cortical stage-specific patterns. Together, our findings provide a cortical characterization of sleep-stage hemodynamic organizations that can serve as a reference for future mechanistic and clinical sleep studies.

papers.title: The Wild West of Nomenclature, Definitions, and Methodologies in Rodent Sleep Scoring.
papers.abstract: Rodent models are essential for investigating the mechanisms and regulation of sleep, yet the field lacks a unified framework for sleep-scoring terminology, definitions, and reporting. Laboratories vary in recording modalities, temporal resolution, staging criteria, and analytical approaches, reflecting both historical practices and the diverse experimental questions addressed using rodent models. Ongoing efforts to harmonize and standardize rodent sleep methodologies are therefore important for improving rigor, reproducibility, and cross-study comparison. However, methodological harmonization also requires a shared vocabulary and clear operational definitions to understand how scoring and analytical approaches are implemented and how methodological choices influence reported outcomes. In this Perspective, we examine variability surrounding fundamental constructs in rodent sleep analysis, including epochs, bouts, segments, fragmentation, and consolidation. We illustrate how choices such as epoch duration and bout initiation, continuation, and termination criteria can alter sleep-stage assignment, bout number and duration, transition frequency, and ultimately the apparent fragmentation or consolidation of sleep. We further distinguish epochs, defined as temporal units receiving vigilance-state assignments, from segments used for signal processing, feature extraction, or data aggregation, and emphasize the importance of defining the specific metrics used to characterize fragmentation and consolidation. Complementing broader efforts to harmonize rodent sleep methodologies, we propose consistent terminology, explicit operational definitions, and minimum reporting practices that make methodological and analytical decisions transparent across recording and scoring approaches. Together, methodological harmonization and a shared vocabulary can strengthen reproducibility, facilitate meaningful cross-study comparison and meta-analysis, and improve translation across experimental models and to human sleep research.

papers.title: P(TMD|OSA) or P(OSA|TMD)? Estimand Heterogeneity in Temporomandibular Disorder-Obstructive Sleep Apnea Comorbidity Research.
papers.abstract: Temporomandibular disorder (TMD) affects an estimated 34% of the global population, with projections suggesting further increases. A genuine but incompletely understood association with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) has been proposed. Reported TMD-OSA co-occurrence varies from 2% to 68% across studies-a range that conflates two different measured quantities (estimands) rather than reflecting a single inconsistent phenomenon. To determine whether apparent heterogeneity in TMD-OSA comorbidity estimates reflects true inconsistency or results from combining non-comparable measurements-studies estimating P(TMD|OSA) versus P(OSA|TMD)-alongside differences in recruitment setting, diagnostic method, severity threshold and control-group presence. A narrative synthesis, not a systematic review, was conducted via a structured PubMed search (inception-July 2026) cross-checked against three existing systematic reviews and meta-analyses. Nine clinic-based, instrument-confirmed studies meeting predefined eligibility criteria were extracted and compared against the population-based literature underlying a 2024 meta-analysis (six studies, pooled odds ratio [OR] 2.61). Wilson 95% confidence intervals were calculated for each proportion; given the small number and clinical heterogeneity of the studies, no formal meta-analytic pooling was attempted. Two of the nine clinic-based studies overlapped with the existing population-based literature (one quantitatively, one qualitatively), so the two literatures are not fully independent, though most clinic-based studies lacked a control group and were excluded from pooling. Reported P(TMD|OSA) ranged from 8.6% [95% CI 4.0-17.5] to 51.7% [41.4-61.9] among studies using RDC/TMD or DC/TMD; one study using a substantially more restrictive definition of treatment-disqualifying TMJ disease reported 2.0% [0.6-7.0] and is not directly comparable to the others. P(OSA|TMD) ranged from 28% [18.0-41.6] to 68% [48.4-82.8] across three studies. The two most rigorously controlled studies did not differ significantly from each other (z = 1.14, p = 0.26), despite one reaching borderline internal significance (p < 0.05) and the other not (p = 0.83). The best-supported conclusion is that these studies measure different quantities, in different populations, using different diagnostic protocols and severity thresholds-not that they are in true biological conflict, though the relative contribution of estimand direction to the overall heterogeneity cannot be quantified from the available studies. Future research should prospectively define which estimand is being measured, apply standardised diagnostic thresholds, adjust for shared confounders (age, sex, BMI) and report control-group characteristics and overlap with existing pooled analyses in full.

papers.title: Examining the network dynamics of core symptoms in Chinese patients with advanced cancer: a diary study.
papers.abstract: Traditional approaches examining isolated symptoms fail to capture dynamic network structures in palliative care. This study aimed to decompose physiological and psychological symptom networks across multiple levels and identify central symptoms that may inform hypothesis-generating targets for future intervention studies in advanced cancer patients. This secondary retrospective longitudinal study utilized diary-based design and multilevel network analysis at a tertiary cancer hospital in mainland China. 166 advanced cancer patients receiving palliative care completed ≥ 20 consecutive daily assessments using standardized PCOC tools: Symptom Assessment Scale (SAS), Palliative Care Problem Severity Score (PCPSS), and Resource Utilisation Group-Activities of Daily Living (RUG-ADL). Multilevel vector autoregressive (mlVAR) models estimated temporal networks (lag-1 effects), contemporaneous networks (same-day associations), and between-subjects networks. Network centrality was quantified using expected influence (EI), with stability evaluated through bootstrap procedures. Time-series stationarity was confirmed via Augmented Dickey-Fuller (ADF) tests, and autocorrelation function (ACF) analysis was conducted to assess temporal persistence patterns across symptom domains. Four distinct network patterns emerged. In SAS networks, nausea showed highest temporal centrality (temEI = 0.102) with cross-lagged associations with appetite loss and bowel distress, while sleep distress (conEI = 0.836) and appetite (conEI = 1.018) were contemporaneously central. PCPSS networks revealed psychological/spiritual issues were associated with subsequent family/carer problems (r = 0.059) with highest between-subjects centrality (0.891). ADL networks identified toileting dependency as temporally central (temEI = 0.199), associated with subsequent changes in functional decline. The comprehensive network highlighted psychological/spiritual problems with strongest temporal influence (temEI = 0.251) and six significant connections, particularly associated with ADL deterioration. Autocorrelation analysis revealed distinct persistence patterns: ADL measures showed strongest persistence; SAS demonstrated moderate decay; PCPSS exhibited scale-specific patterns with psychological/spiritual concerns showing greater persistence (0.814 → 0.258) than pain (0.544 → 0.020). This study identified distinct symptom network patterns across temporal, contemporaneous, and between-subjects levels. Findings provide preliminary evidence that may guide future intervention studies targeting central symptoms to investigate potential cascading effects and optimize monitoring strategies based on symptom persistence characteristics.

papers.title: Body weight history from young adulthood and subsequent blood pressure trajectories in a Japanese employment-based health-check cohort: a retrospective longitudinal study.
papers.abstract: Whether long-term body weight history across adulthood, rather than body weight at a single time point, is associated with later blood pressure (BP) trajectories remains uncertain. We examined this association in a large longitudinal health checkup cohort. We analyzed repeated systolic and diastolic blood pressure measurements from 406,814 participants in a Japanese employment-based health-check cohort using sex-stratified linear mixed-effects models with age-by-group interactions and adjustment for sleep, exercise habits, physical activity, and walking speed. Participants were classified into three groups: history of underweight (BMI < 18.5 kg/m² at least once; n = 80,890), normal weight only (BMI 18.5 to < 25.0 kg/m² throughout the 20s; n = 228,343), and history of obesity (BMI ≥ 25.0 kg/m² at least once; n = 97,581). Sensitivity analyses among 402,651 participants additionally adjusted for eating speed, breakfast skipping, and late-evening meals. The underweight-history and obesity-history groups were further subdivided by the proportion of follow-up time spent underweight or obese (0-25%, 25-50%, 50-75%, and 75-100%). Participants with a history of obesity during their 20s showed higher BP trajectories than those with normal weight only, and these differences increased with age. In contrast, participants with a history of underweight showed lower BP trajectories than the normal-weight-only group. Age-by-group interactions were significant in women and men for both systolic and diastolic BP (all P < 0.001). Additional adjustment for eating behaviors had minimal influence on these associations. In the nine-group analysis, the groups with 50-75% and 75-100% of follow-up time spent obese showed higher BP trajectories than the normal-weight-only group, whereas the groups with 50-75% and 75-100% of follow-up time spent underweight showed lower BP trajectories. These findings suggest that shorter durations of obesity and underweight may be associated with BP trajectories closer to those of the normal-weight-only group. Overall, long-term body weight history may be more informative than body weight at a single time point when evaluating later BP burden.

papers.title: Assessment of triglyceride-glucose index and its modified indices in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus and their relationship with dinner timing.
papers.abstract: Type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is associated with various micro- and macrovascular complications that lead to premature morbidity and mortality. Insulin resistance disrupts glucose disposal, elevates hepatic glucose output, and accelerates β-cell dysfunction, thereby increasing cardiometabolic risk. The triglyceride-glucose (TyG) index and its anthropometric derivatives provide simple and cost-effective surrogate measures of insulin resistance. Habitual late dinner timing may impair glucose and lipid metabolism due to circadian variation. However, the relationship between TyG, TyG modified indices, and chrononutrition behaviour such as dinner timing remains limited in adults with T2DM. The cross-sectional study conducted in Vadodara city, India included 441 adults aged 35-60 years with T2DM of less than five years' duration and not requiring insulin therapy. Participants were categorized as early (< 21:00; n = 200) or late (≥ 21:00; n = 241)diners. Anthropometric measurements were obtained using standardized protocols, body composition was assessed by bioelectrical impedance analysis, and dietary intake was evaluated using a 3-day 24-hour dietary recall and food frequency questionnaire. Biochemical parameters were obtained from recent medical records (< 3 days). Data were analyzed using SPSS version 24. Mean age of participants was 49.3 ± 7.1years and 232 (52.6%)were males. The mean values of TyG, TyG-BMI, TyG-WC (waist circumference), TyG-WHr (waist-to-hip ratio), and TyG-WHtr (waist-to-height ratio) were 4.95 ± 0.24, 135.58 ± 23.14, 478.72 ± 62.82, 4.58 ± 0.47, and 2.98 ± 0.39,respectively. TyG, TyG-BMI, TyG-WC, TyG-WHr, and TyG-WHtr increased progressively across quartiles (all p < 0.001) from 4.64 ± 0.11 to 5.26 ± 0.12, 106.23 ± 9.43 to 165.29 ± 12.49, 400.86 ± 25.57 to 561.67 ± 31.30, 4.04 ± 0.17 to 5.21 ± 0.27, and 2.51 ± 0.15 to 3.51 ± 0.24, respectively, accompanied by progressively adverse lipemic, glycaemic, and adiposity profiles. TyG index showed the strongest differentiation for biochemical markers triglycerides (F = 229.870), TG/HDL ratio (F = 133.410), fasting blood glucose (F = 91.928), and HbA1c (F = 32.240). The modified indices showed strongest differentiation for their respective anthropometric components: TyG-BMI for BMI (F = 638.905), TyG-WC for WC (F = 457.098), TyG-WHr for WHr (F = 276.633), and TyG-WHtr for WHtr (F = 398.272). Beyond these formula-derived relations, TyG-BMI showed the strongest differentiation for visceral fat percentage (F = 117.639), TyG-WHr for HDL-C (F = 34.643), and TyG-WHtr for muscle percentage (F = 17.395). Participants with late dinner timing had significantly higher index values than early diners (all p < 0.001), with moderate effect sizes (Cohen's d = 0.55-0.77). The largest between-group differences were observed for TyG (Cohen's d = 0.77), TyG-WHtr (0.76),and TyG-WC (0.75). Multiple linear regression analyses showed that late dinner timing was an independent positive predictor of TyG (β = 0.365), TyG-BMI (β = 0.265), TyG-WC (β = 0.350), TyG-WHr (β = 0.308), and TyG-WHtr (β = 0.342) after adjusting for sex, age, energy intake, and physical activity (all p < 0.001), with the models explaining 7-15% of the variability in these indices. Partial (r = 0.26-0.37) and part (r = 0.25-0.36) correlation showed its independent relation with indices after adjustment. Female sex was significantly negatively related with TyG-WC (β=-0.112) and significantly positively related with TyG-WHtr (β = 0.133). Increasing age was significantly positively related with TyG-WHr (β = 0.090) and TyG-WHtr (β = 0.093). Physical activity showed a weak inverse, although non-significant, relation with anthropometry related TyG indices (TyG-BMI, TyG-WC, and TyG-WHtr). Habitual late dinner timing was independently related with higher TyG and modified TyG indices. Not applicable.

papers.title: Dairy intake and sleep duration and quality: a systematic review and dose-response meta-analysis of observational and interventional studies.
papers.abstract: Due to the complexities of modern life, sleep disorders have become prevalent, leading to a number of physical and mental health issues. This meta-analysis was conducted to explore the association between dairy consumption and sleep parameters. Following a database search, 29 citations (25 observational and 4 trials) were included in the meta-analysis. In observational studies, a dose-response association was observed between dairy ingestion and better sleep quality and duration. Consumption of milk had a linear association with good sleep quality at doses up to 2 servings/day. The estimated reduction in risk of poor sleep quality was 15% for each serving increase in milk consumption (OR = 0.85; 95% CIs: 0.76, 0.94, P = 0.001). Consumption of dairy also showed an association with good sleep quality at doses up to 1.5 servings/day. However, higher doses of milk (> 3 servings/day) and dairy (> 2 servings/day) showed a trend towards an increased risk of poor sleep quality. For short sleep duration, consumption of milk in doses > 0.7 servings/day showed a positive association with sleep duration. The highest vs. lowest analysis also showed an association between yogurt, but not cheese, consumption and sleep duration. In trials, dairy consumption indicated a significant improvement in sleep quality (mean difference = -0.49; 95% CIs: -0.92, -0.05, P = 0.031), a finding which was confirmed by dose-response analysis. Overall, results showed a dose-response association between dairy and especially milk and better sleep quality and duration.

papers.title: Nonrestorative sleep, sleep duration, and chronotype in relation to depression: a cross-sectional study in Japan.
papers.abstract: Nonrestorative sleep (NRS), sleep duration, and chronotype are associated with depression. However, the combined association between NRS and sleep duration or chronotype and depression remains unclear. Thus, this study aimed to investigate the association between depression and combinations of NRS and sleep duration or chronotype. This cross-sectional study used data from the Japan "Society and new Tobacco" Internet Survey in 2025, including participants aged ≥ 20 years. Depression was defined as self-reported currently having depression under medical care with medication. Participants were classified according to the frequency of NRS, defined as a lack of subjective sleep recovery, sleep duration, and chronotype, assessed based on the sleep-corrected midpoint of sleep on free days. Multivariate logistic regression was used to assess the association between depression and combinations of NRS and sleep duration or chronotype. Of the 20,951 participants, 658 reported current depression. In those with NRS ≥ 3 times/week, the odds of depression were higher across all sleep durations, with sleeping ≥ 9 h showing the highest (adjusted odds ratio [aOR], 8.42; 95% confidence interval [CI], 5.13-13.79), compared with those without NRS who slept 7-8 h. Among those without NRS, sleeping 6-7 h had the lowest odds of depression (aOR, 0.56; 95% CI, 0.32-0.99), whereas sleeping < 5 h and sleeping 8-9 h were associated with higher odds (aOR 2.06, 95% CI: 1.04-4.06 and aOR 1.97, 95% CI: 1.21-3.19, respectively). Frequent NRS was associated with higher odds across all chronotypes; however, chronotype was not significantly associated with depression among those without NRS. Frequent NRS is consistently associated with depression across all sleep durations and chronotypes. Assessing NRS frequency may provide additional information beyond sleep duration or chronotype to identify adults at risk of depression.

papers.title: The role of bilateral temporal poles activity mediating the association between anxiety symptoms and sleep problems in children with autism spectrum disorder.
papers.abstract: Sleep problems and anxiety symptoms frequently occur in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD). This investigation sought to examine the shared neural mechanisms that underly the co-occurrence of anxiety symptoms and sleep problems in this population. A total of 163 children with ASD were recruited. The anxiety symptoms and sleep problems were assessed through the Child Behavior Checklist and Children's Sleep Habits Questionnaire, respectively. Resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging(rs-fMRI) was utilized to compute the amplitude of low-frequency fluctuations (ALFF). Mediation analyses were conducted to examine the interrelationships among ALFF, anxiety symptoms, and sleep problems. Sleep problems scores were positively linked to anxiety scores. ALFF in bilateral temporal poles were positively linked to anxiety scores. Mediation analyses revealed the right superior temporal pole mediated the pathway from sleep problems to anxiety symptoms. The left middle temporal pole exhibited a significant mediating effect in both directions of anxiety-sleep relationship. These findings enhance comprehension of neurobiological processes that underlie the co-occurrence of anxiety symptoms and sleep problems, while identifying promising targets for subsequent clinical therapeutic approaches. As all rs-fMRI scans were performed under sedation, our results cannot be generalized to unsedated children or those scanned with different sedative protocols.

papers.title: Investigating working memory and brain activation in major depressive disorder with and without insomnia: insights from functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS).
papers.abstract: Major depressive disorder (MDD) frequently coexists with insomnia, a comorbidity that exacerbates cognitive deficits, particularly in working memory (WM). While previous research has established links between insomnia and impaired brain function, the barin functional indicators associated with WM deficits in MDD patients with insomnia remain unclear. This study explores cortical activation patterns in MDD patients with and without insomnia using functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). A total of 55 MDD patients with insomnia and 67 without insomnia were recruited. Cortical activation during WM tasks was assessed using fNIRS, focusing on oxygenated hemoglobin (Oxy-Hb) concentration changes. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), depression severity was assessed using the Hamilton Depression Scale (HAMD), and cognitive function was assessed using the Repeatable Battery for the Assessment of Neuropsychological Status (RBANS). MDD patients with insomnia exhibited lower RBANS scores and reduced accuracy in medium-load WM tasks compared to non-insomnia patients. Additionally, fNIRS analysis revealed diminished Oxy-Hb concentrations in the bilateral dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC) during medium-load tasks and in the left DLPFC during high-load tasks. Correlation analyses indicated that immediate memory scores negatively correlated with left DLPFC and bilateral medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) activation during medium-load tasks, while task accuracy negatively correlated with bilateral mPFC activation (p < 0.05). The presence of insomnia in MDD is associated with exacerbated WM deficits and altered prefrontal cortical activation, particularly in tasks with increased cognitive demand. These findings provide potential neurofunctional reference indicators, which may help offer auxiliary assessment means for MDD patients with insomnia. In addition, the sensitivity of fNIRS in detecting these neural brain activation differences suggest it may have potential as an exploratory screening tool for identifying subtypes of depression.

papers.title: Clinical outcomes following ultrasound-guided posterior tibial nerve pulsed radiofrequency combined with perineural injection in refractory restless legs syndrome.
papers.abstract: Restless legs syndrome (RLS) is a chronic sensorimotor disorder, and a subset of patients remains symptomatic despite pharmacological treatment. Pulsed radiofrequency (PRF) is a minimally invasive neuromodulation technique that can modulate peripheral afferent pathways without causing thermal nerve injury. This study evaluated the short-term clinical outcomes following ultrasound-guided PRF targeting the posterior tibial nerve (PTN) combined with perineural dexamethasone and lidocaine injection in patients with refractory RLS. In this retrospective observational study, the medical records of 30 patients with refractory RLS who underwent bilateral ultrasound-guided PTN PRF followed by perineural dexamethasone and lidocaine injection as part of routine clinical practice were reviewed. Restlessness severity, RLS symptom severity, and self-reported sleep disturbance were assessed using the Visual Analog Scale (VAS), International Restless Legs Syndrome Rating Scale (IRLS-RS), and Jenkins Sleep Scale (JSS), respectively, at baseline and at 1 and 3 months after the procedure. Thirty patients were included in the study. IRLS-RS scores decreased from 28.23 ± 3.73 at baseline to 12.23 ± 3.41 at 1 month and 17.67 ± 4.08 at 3 months (p < 0.001), corresponding to mean reductions of 16.00 and 10.56 points, respectively. VAS scores also decreased significantly from 7.33 ± 0.75 at baseline to 3.23 ± 1.22 at 1 month and 4.60 ± 1.10 at 3 months (p < 0.001). JSS scores improved from 12.17 ± 1.76 at baseline to 7.80 ± 2.61 at 3 months (p < 0.001). Ultrasound-guided PTN PRF combined with perineural dexamethasone and lidocaine was associated with significant short-term improvements in RLS symptom severity, restlessness, and self-reported sleep disturbance in patients with refractory RLS. These findings suggest that PTN-targeted peripheral neuromodulation may represent a potential minimally invasive treatment approach in selected patients; however, prospective controlled studies are needed to confirm these preliminary findings and to clarify the independent contribution of PRF.

papers.title: Tau conveys intrinsic hyperactivity of VTA dopamine neurons but an inability to sustain burst firing.
papers.abstract: Ventral tegmental area (VTA) dopamine is implicated in neuropsychiatric symptoms in Alzheimer's disease (AD). Mouse AD models show dopamine neuron hyperexcitability, but also decreased dopamine release and disrupted reward learning. Specific roles for amyloid and tau have not been determined. We investigated the triggers of disrupted dopamine neuron firing in mouse AD models: 3xTg-AD (amyloid+tau), APPNL -G-F (amyloid only), and a viral model expressing pathogenic human tau (p-tau). 3xTg-AD dopamine neurons showed less bursting in vivo, yet faster non-burst spiking. In ex vivo slices, these neurons showed impaired ability to sustain firing during depolarization, which we mimicked with depolarizing current in wild-type neurons. Inducing p-tau expression similarly caused firing aberrations, effects not recapitulated in APPNL-G-F neurons. P-tau induces hyperexcitability within individual dopamine neurons, but this likely reduces transmission in vivo through impaired bursting. Further studies investigating dopamine release in vivo may elucidate timepoints for early AD intervention.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association

papers.title: Correlation and Agreement Between Bispectral Index Monitoring and Quantitative EEG in Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage.
papers.abstract: Delayed cerebral ischemia (DCI) is a major cause of poor outcome after aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH). Continuous EEG can predict DCI but is resource intensive. Processed EEG monitors such as the bispectral index (BIS) are simpler, yet their relationship with quantitative EEG (qEEG) parameters remains unclear. We evaluated the correlation and agreement between BIS and qEEG in aSAH. Single-center prospective study of adults with aSAH who underwent two 30-min routine EEG recordings with simultaneous bilateral BIS monitoring (within 72 h of admission and on days 4-7). qEEG parameters were extracted from frontal channels adjacent to the BIS sensor and from full-montage EEG recordings. Prespecified comparisons included BIS total power (BIS-tpw), spectral edge frequency (BIS-sef), and BIS value (BIS-v) with corresponding qEEG measures. Correlation and agreement were assessed using correlation coefficients, intraclass correlation, concordance analysis, regression methods, and Bland-Altman approaches. Exploratory analyses evaluated the DCI interaction in BIS-qEEG associations and concordance for DCI detection. Sixty-four patients contributed 248 paired BIS-qEEG observations. Prespecified parameter pairs showed moderate-to-strong correlations (ρ > 0.6), particularly between BIS-tpw and qEEG power measures and between BIS-sef and qEEG-sef. Agreement analyses were fair to good for BIS-tpw and BIS-sef [absolute intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) up to ~0.75; consistency ICCs ≥ 0.80]. In contrast, BIS-v showed weak correlations, poor agreement, and substantial between-patient variability. Associations were strongest with frontal qEEG parameters, whereas correlations with full-montage qEEG measures were moderate. DCI was associated with consistent BIS-qEEG differences and fair-to-good concordance. BIS-derived parameters, particularly BIS-tpw and BIS-sef, were associated with qEEG measures of spectral power and frequency in aSAH. In contrast, BIS-v showed weaker and less reliable relationships with qEEG metrics. BIS monitoring may provide complementary bedside electrophysiological trends when continuous EEG is unavailable but should not be considered interchangeable with qEEG.

papers.title: Spreading Depolarization after Traumatic Brain Injury and Subdural Hematoma: A Context-Specific Framework for Recognition and Clinical Interpretation without Electrocorticography.
papers.abstract: Spreading depolarization (SD) is a near-complete breakdown of transmembrane ion gradients that propagates through gray matter and imposes substantial metabolic stress. Direct subdural electrocorticography (ECoG) has established SD as a common and prognostically relevant secondary injury process in a subset of patients with severe traumatic brain injury (TBI), whereas a smaller body of literature implicates SD in recurrent transient neurological symptoms after subdural hematoma (SDH), particularly chronic SDH (cSDH) and after hematoma evacuation. These populations should not, however, be treated as a single clinical syndrome. In this narrative review, we distinguish three context-specific evidence domains: (1) directly monitored SD in severe or surgical TBI, (2) SD as a plausible contributor to recurrent stereotyped focal symptoms after cSDH/SDH evacuation, and (3) imaging correlates of prior SD-associated spreading ischemia. We emphasize that routine scalp electroencephalogram (EEG) does not diagnose SD in patients with intact skull, that seizures and SD can coexist, and that cortical-predominant or laminar ischemic injury on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) can support but cannot establish active SD. We propose a context-specific clinical approach for centers without ECoG that focuses on recognizing when SD should enter the differential, defines what conventional EEG and imaging can and cannot establish, and identifies situations in which direct monitoring may be valuable. Standard physiological optimization remains foundational in severe acute brain injury but is not an SD-specific treatment recommendation. Ketamine can suppress ECoG-confirmed SD, whereas evidence for nimodipine, memantine, topiramate, and other candidate therapies remains context dependent or investigational. Prospective validation is required before unmonitored clinical patterns are used as treatment triggers.

papers.title: The neuroscience of delirium: a perfect storm for acute brain dysfunction.
papers.abstract: Delirium is a frequent and distressing neuropsychiatric syndrome characterized by acute disturbances of attention, awareness and cognition. Delirium emerges in response to diverse medical insults, particularly in hospitalized patients. Despite its high prevalence and association with accelerated cognitive decline, dementia and mortality, the neurobiology of delirium remains incompletely understood, and there are no treatments for delirium. Evidence from electrophysiology, neuroimaging, biomarkers and emerging animal models has begun to clarify the pathophysiological mechanisms underlying delirium. Delirium can be conceptualized as the interaction of acute systemic or cerebral stressors with pre-existing vulnerabilities, creating a 'perfect storm' for brain dysfunction. Generalized electroencephalographic slowing and network disintegration are convergent signatures across diverse types of delirium. Disruptions in neuromodulatory systems, energy metabolism and neuroimmune signalling may underlie impairment of large-scale brain function. The mechanisms that drive acute delirium may also contribute to subsequent brain injury and long-term decline, compounding its broad personal and societal impact.

papers.title: Aging disrupts sleep-driven brain fluid flow.
The aging human brain exhibits reduced hemodynamic and cerebrospinal fluid flow waves during sleep.
papers.abstract: Aging reduces the quality and quantity of sleep, and sleep disruption is predictive of neurodegeneration and cognitive decline. Sleep loss could affect brain health through disruption of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) circulation, which is important for brain homeostasis. In young adults, large CSF flow waves appear during non-rapid eye movement sleep; however, whether sleep-dependent brain fluid physiology changes in aging is not known. Here we imaged large-scale CSF flow and hemodynamics in young (18-39 years) and older (60-84 years) adults during nighttime sleep. Sleep-dependent CSF flow was reduced in older adults, and was linked to reduced EEG slow wave power, decreased global hemodynamic oscillations and gray matter atrophy. Using sensory and vasoactive stimuli to drive CSF flow, we found that both neural and cerebrovascular changes contributed to this disruption. These results demonstrate reduced CSF flow during sleep in human aging, before disease onset, and identify parallel neural and hemodynamic mechanisms contributing to this decline.

papers.title: Suppression of neuronal eEF2K alleviates cognitive deficits and apathy-like behavior in APP/PS1 AD model mice.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a complex neurodegenerative disorder characterized by synaptic failure, cognitive impairment and neuropsychiatric symptoms (NPS). Apathy is the most common NPS seen in AD patients, and its underlying mechanisms remain unknown. Here, we investigated the roles of neuronal eukaryotic elongation factor 2 (eEF2) phosphorylation (by its kinase eEF2K) in AD-associated cognitive deficits and NPS. We performed a series of experiments using a multidisciplinary approach including genetics, behavioral assays, synaptic electrophysiology, and unbiased proteomics. The results demonstrated that neuron-specific inhibition of eEF2K and eEF2 phosphorylation can alleviate cognitive deficits, synaptic plasticity impairments, and apathy-like behavior in aged APP/PS1 AD model mice. Our findings indicate the therapeutic potential of targeting the eEF2K signaling in the treatment of dementia and NPS in AD and related dementias (ADRDs).

papers.title: Vagus-Hepatic-Creatine axis modulates manic-like behaviors via hippocampal MMP19 upregulation in bipolar disorder.
papers.abstract: Bipolar disorder (BD) is associated with pronounced alterations in peripheral creatine kinase levels; however, the mechanistic basis of this phenomenon remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we conducted a translational study combining clinical assessments in 55 patients with major depressive disorder, 57 BD patients, and 55 healthy controls, alongside sleep deprivation-induced manic-like mouse models. Our findings revealed significantly elevated peripheral creatine concentrations in both BD patients and model mice, which correlated with increased hepatic expression of guanidinoacetate N-methyltransferase (GAMT), a rate-limiting enzyme in creatine biosynthesis. Behavioral experiments in mice showed that exogenous creatine supplementation recapitulated manic-like phenotypes, whereas administration of the creatine analogue β-guanidinopropionic acid (β-GPA) or surgical subdiaphragmatic vagotomy effectively ameliorated these aberrant behaviors. Mechanistically, peripherally derived creatine was found to modulate neural activity independently of blood-brain barrier penetration, acting instead through interleukin-1α (IL-1α)-mediated inflammatory signaling. Transcriptomic analyses further identified hippocampal matrix metalloproteinase-19 (MMP19) as a critical downstream effector, and genetic knockdown experiments confirmed its indispensability in the expression of manic-like behaviors. Collectively, these results delineate a previously unrecognized vagus-liver-creatine-hippocampal axis in BD pathophysiology, highlighting peripheral creatine metabolic routes as actionable targets for therapeutic intervention. Overall, this work provides compelling evidence that peripheral metabolic disturbances can drive central nervous system dysfunction via neuroimmune crosstalk, offering a new conceptual framework for understanding mood disorder etiology.

papers.title: Long-term stability and effectiveness of maxillomandibular advancement for obstructive sleep apnea: systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Maxillomandibular advancement (MMA) surgery has been shown to effectively increase airway volume and reduce apnoea severity in adult patients with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA). This study aimed to evaluate the long-term stability and effectiveness of MMA in managing OSA. Following PROSPERO registration (CRD42021238944), major databases and grey literature were searched through May 2025 for studies with ≥2-year follow-up. The review was conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook and reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 guidelines. Study quality was assessed using the Methodological Index for Non-Randomised Studies (MINORS). Meta-analyses were performed on skeletal parameters, Sella-Nasion-Point A (SNA) and Sella-Nasion-Point B (SNB) angles, and the Apnoea-Hypopnea Index (AHI). The certainty of the evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Of 1299 articles retrieved, 34 underwent full-text review, and 14 met the inclusion criteria. Assessment using the MINORS tool revealed moderate concerns in a few studies, while the overall certainty of evidence was downgraded to low. Meta-analysis showed significant post-operative skeletal changes: SNA angle increased by a mean of 6.29° (95% CI: 4.90-7.67°) and remained stable at 6.18° (95% CI: 4.86-7.51°) during long-term follow-up. SNB increased by 4.80° (95% CI: 3.15-6.45°) and remained stable at 5.38° (95% CI: 3.04-7.71°). AHI decreased significantly by 40.30 events/hour (95% CI: 32.23-48.37) in the long term. MMA surgery was associated with substantial long-term improvement in AHI and generally stable skeletal outcomes among adult OSA patients. However, substantial between-study heterogeneity and the low certainty of evidence limit the precision and generalisability of the pooled estimates. Further well-designed prospective studies with standardised reporting and long-term follow-up are warranted.

papers.title: Coordination-Chemistry-Directed Nanofluidic Ion-Channel Engineering Enables Trimodal Self-Powered, Colorimetric, and Wireless Humidity Transduction in a Wet-Spun Biopolymer Fiber.
papers.abstract: Wearable humidity monitoring is central to personalized healthcare, yet few nanostructured platforms unite colorimetric, self-powered, and wireless transduction within a single fiber. Here, a hydrochromic fiber is fabricated by wet-spinning a sodium alginate (SA)/tricarboxylated bacterial cellulose (TBC) dope into a CoCl2 coagulation bath. Shear-aligned TBC nanorods form anisotropic ion-transport nanochannels, while coordinated Co2+ ions act as both ionic cross-linkers and hydrochromic centers, switching reversibly between tetrahedral (blue, dry) and octahedral (pink, wet) geometries for naked-eye humidity readout. Paired with Ag and Zn wire electrodes, the resulting galvanic cell delivers a peak open-circuit voltage of ∼900 mV at 91% relative humidity (RH), a peak sensitivity of 13.75 mV %RH-1, response/recovery times of 1.1/1.28 s, and stable operation over 200 wet-dry cycles across 10°C-70°C. Molecular dynamics simulations show that water uptake reorganizes the hydrogen-bond network and drives Co2+/Cl- transport from a sub-diffusive to a diffusive regime. Interfaced with a Bluetooth Low Energy microcontroller, the fiber enables real-time wireless tracking of respiration, including sleep apnea events, and diaper-wetness alerts; a Random Forest classifier discriminates six respiratory states with 99.2% accuracy in a single-subject proof-of-concept test. This coordination-chemistry strategy is transferable to other metal-biopolymer systems.

papers.title: Scalable Sleep Apnoea Endotype Profiling and Estimated Oral Appliance Treatment Response in a Large Clinical Cohort.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) pathogenesis is heterogeneous with important contributions from impaired upper airway anatomy and at least three key non-anatomical endotypes. Detailed physiology assessments in a relatively small number of well-characterized participants indicate wide interindividual variability in pharyngeal collapsibility and that ~70% have impairment in one or more non-anatomical endotype. In this study, we applied recently developed models that use standard clinical and polysomnography data to estimate OSA endotypes and oral appliance therapy response in a large clinical population. OSA endotypes and oral appliance therapy responses were estimated using standard sleep study outputs and clinical data (age and BMI) from > 6500 consecutive home-based diagnostic studies with an Apnoea/Hypopnea Index (AHI) > 5 events/h (Sleep Profiler PSG-Advanced Brain Monitoring). The proportion of participants who were estimated to have impairment in one or more OSA endotypes was calculated according to previously published physiological cutoffs. On average, participants (39% female) had moderately severe OSA (AHI = 28 ± 23 events/h [Mean ± SD]), were middle aged (49 ± 16 years) and obese (BMI = 31 ± 7 kg/m2). 29% were estimated to have only mild anatomical compromise. 23% had poor dilator muscles, 31% high loop gain and 29% had a low arousal threshold. 62% had severe ("bad") impairment in one or more non-anatomical endotypes. ~60% were predicted to respond to oral appliance therapy. These novel data highlight the heterogeneity of OSA in a large clinical OSA patient population and the feasibility for endotype-informed precision medicine for OSA via application of novel physiology-based algorithms using home sleep study recordings at scale.

papers.title: Cold Polymerization Enables a Hybrid Hydrogel for Coupling Electronic Devices to Skin.
papers.abstract: Wearable electronic devices monitoring physiological signals from skin generate heat that can lead to skin irritation, burns, and reduced device lifespan. Current heat-managing materials involve trade-offs in performance, flexibility, strength, and biocompatibility. Here, we report a heat-managing adhesive hydrogel for wearables that is simultaneously transparent to ultrasound waves, available for electronic recording, conformable to skin, durable and biocompatible. Our hydrogel integrates biomacromolecule gelatin with synthetic polyacrylamide. A cold crosslinking strategy is proposed to kinetically trap the gelatin-acrylamide mixture in a physical gel state prior to photocrosslinking, effectively preventing otherwise phase separation and yielding a transmitted and structurally stable hybrid hydrogel. In our hydrogel, gelatin absorbs heat through gel-sol transition, while its chemical crosslinking with polyacrylamide strengthens the material. The resulting hydrogel is an excellent coupling pad for ultrasound imaging and electroencephalogram recording, and functions as a strain sensor for monitoring human motion. This hybrid material system could be a universal material form coupling rigid devices to skin or coupling stretchable electronic devices to skin.

papers.title: Residential pest signs, housing conditions, and perceived sleep disturbance attributed to pest worry among U.S. households.
papers.abstract: Residential pests are housing-related environmental hazards, but their relationship with perceived sleep disturbance remains poorly characterized. This study examined residential pest signs and sleep disturbance attributed to pest worry and whether housing and socioeconomic conditions differentiated this burden among U.S. households. Data were from Split-Sample Group 2 of the 2023 American Housing Survey. Pest-related sleep disturbance was defined as reporting that worry about pests frequently prevented household members from obtaining sufficient sleep. Survey-weighted analyses examined cockroach and rodent signs, housing and socioeconomic characteristics, pest-sleep concordance, and standardized predicted probabilities across residential contexts. Perceived pest-related sleep disturbance affected 1.1% (95% CI: 0.9%-1.2%) of U.S. households, representing an estimated 1.31 million households. Among pest-exposed households, 3.57% (95% CI: 2.92%-4.22%) reported pest-related sleep disturbance, whereas approximately 96% did not. Among households reporting pest-related sleep disturbance, 72.0% (95% CI: 64.8%-79.2%) reported cockroach or rodent signs. Within pest-exposed households, moderate housing inadequacy (aOR = 2.68), renter occupancy (aOR = 3.74), and income <100% of the federal poverty level (aOR = 5.57) were associated with greater odds of pest-related sleep disturbance. For households reporting both pest types, standardized probabilities ranged from 1.72% under favorable residential conditions to 45.17% under adverse conditions. Perceived pest-related sleep disturbance affects more than one million U.S. households, but pest signs do not uniformly correspond with reported sleep disruption. Pest-attributed sleep disturbance varies substantially across housing and socioeconomic contexts and should be interpreted as perceived sleep disturbance specifically attributed to pest worry rather than objective or general sleep disturbance.

papers.title: Stability of actigraphy-derived sleep and rest-activity rhythm estimates in the UK Biobank.
papers.abstract: Assess stability of sleep and rest-activity rhythm parameters derived from a 7-day accelerometry protocol and evaluate implications for estimating sleep-disease associations. UK Biobank cohort participants (n = 3166, 51% female, 57% BMI≥25) recorded up to 7 days of accelerometry at baseline; 2-5 years later, 4 assessments were conducted at 3-month intervals. GGIR (version 3.0.6) parameters included sleep duration, midpoint of sleep, sleep onset, wake after sleep onset, social jetlag, interdaily stability, intradaily variability, and extended cosinor-derived features (e.g., acrotime, MESOR). Intraclass correlation coefficients of 7-day aggregates characterized follow-up stability of sleep and rest-activity rhythm parameters over 3 months, 12 months, and 2-5 years (long-term). Intraclass correlation coefficients were generally consistent across follow-up. Long-term intraclass correlation coefficients included sleep duration: 0.66 (95% CI: 0.64, 0.68), midpoint of sleep: 0.57 (0.55, 0.60), sleep onset: 0.61 (0.58, 0.63), wake after sleep onset: 0.64 (0.61, 0.66), social jetlag: 0.19 (0.14, 0.24), interdaily stability: 0.77 (0.75, 0.78), and intradaily variability: 0.25 (0.22, 0.29). Parameters with lower stability evidenced substantial regression coefficient attenuation (e.g., ~80% for social jetlag). Most sleep/rest-activity rhythm parameters demonstrated moderate-to-high stability, supporting single assessment protocols as a reasonable approximation of "usual" sleep over 2-5 years. Less stable features may require repeated assessment or statistical calibration to avoid biased effect estimates.

papers.title: Assessing the effects of parental smoking on sleep health in preschool children: A multidimensional approach.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveSleep is essential for children's physical growth, cognitive development, and emotional well-being. Various factors can influence sleep duration. Parental smoking is a significant environmental factor that may influence children's sleep patterns, yet its effects on sleep duration and quality remain unclear. This study aimed to explore the impact of parental secondhand smoke exposure on children's sleep duration and quality using multidimensional clinical sleep data.MethodsFirst, we conducted a cross-sectional study comparing two groups of preschool children from our hospital: one group with smoking parents and another with nonsmoking parents. Data were collected from 223 children, and polysomnography was used to measure total sleep time, nonrapid eye movement sleep, rapid eye movement sleep, and other sleep parameters. We then analyzed data from the National Sleep Research Resource database, which includes information on sleep and smoking behaviors among preschool-aged children. A total of 301 children with complete data on sleep duration and smoking-related variables were included. R software was used for statistical analysis.ResultsIn the local preschool cohort, 95 children were included, with 40 in the nonsmoking parental group and 55 in the parental smoking group. Parental smoking was not independently associated with total sleep time or sleep efficiency. However, it was associated with a higher burden of sleep-related respiratory events, including hypopnea, obstructive apnea, and total respiratory events; the adjusted rate ratio for total events was 2.27 (95% CI: 1.82-2.83). In the sensitivity analysis covering the full local age range, the association with total respiratory events persisted. In the National Sleep Research Resource database, 104 of 301 children (34.6%) lived with at least one current household smoker. Current household smoking was associated with age-specific short sleep in the fully adjusted model (odds ratio (OR) = 2.00; 95% CI: 1.14-3.53; p = 0.016) and with a lower percentage of N3/stage 3-4 sleep (β, -2.32% points; 95% CI: -4.40 to -0.23; p = 0.029).ConclusionsOur analysis suggests that parental smoking may not have a significant direct impact on children's sleep duration in clinical cohorts from our hospital. Instead, the findings suggest that secondhand smoke exposure may be associated with specific dimensions of sleep quality, particularly sleep-related respiratory event burden in the local preschool cohort and age-specific short sleep and reduced slow-wave sleep in the National Sleep Research Resource cohort.
